title.zh: 卷七十四 志第二十七 律曆七
title.raw: 卷七十四 志第二十七 律曆七 Volume 74 Treatises 27: Measures and Calendar 7

sentences.zh: 明天曆

translations.literal: The Tianli Calendar
translations.idiomatic: The Tianli Calendar

sentences.zh: 調日法朔余、周天分、鬥分、歲差、日度母附

translations.literal: Appendix on adjusting the day divisor, new-moon remainder, circuit-of-heaven parts, Dipper fraction, annual difference, and day-degree mother
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Adjusting the Day Divisor, New-Moon Remainder, Circuit-of-Heaven Parts, Dipper Fraction, Precession, and Day-Degree Mother

sentences.zh: 造曆之法，必先立元，元正然後定日法，法定然後度周天，以定分、至，三者有程，則曆可成矣。

translations.literal: The method for making a calendar must first establish the origin; when the origin is correct, then fix the day divisor; when the divisor is fixed, then measure the circuit of heaven to fix the solstitial limits—when these three have their measure, the calendar can be completed.
translations.idiomatic: To construct a calendar, one must first establish the epoch. Once the epoch is settled, the day divisor is fixed; once the divisor is fixed, the circuit of heaven is measured to determine the solstitial points. When all three have their proper measures, the calendar can be completed.

sentences.zh: 日者，積余成之；

translations.literal: Days are formed by accumulating remainders;
translations.idiomatic: Days arise from the accumulation of fractional remainders;

sentences.zh: 度者，積分成之。

translations.literal: degrees are formed by accumulating parts.
translations.idiomatic: and degrees arise from the accumulation of fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 蓋日月始離，初行生分，積分成日。

translations.literal: For when sun and moon first separate, their initial motion generates parts, and accumulated parts become days.
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon first separate, their initial motion generates fractional parts, and those accumulated parts become days.

sentences.zh: 自《四分曆》洎古之六曆，皆以九百四十為日法。

translations.literal: From the Quarter-Remainder Calendar down through the six ancient calendars, all used nine hundred forty as the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: From the Quarter-Remainder Calendar through the six ancient calendars, the day divisor was uniformly 940.

sentences.zh: 率由日行一度，經三百六十五日四分之一，是為周天；

translations.literal: The rate derives from the sun's traveling one degree, passing through three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter days—this is the circuit of heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The rate assumes the sun moves one degree per day through 365¼ days, the full circuit of heaven;

sentences.zh: 月行十三度十九分之七，經二十九日有餘，與日相會，是為朔策。

translations.literal: the moon travels thirteen and seven-nineteenths degrees, passing through twenty-nine-odd days until it meets the sun—this is the new-moon cycle.
translations.idiomatic: while the moon moves 13° 7/19 per synodic month (~29+ days) until it meets the sun—that is the new-moon cycle.

sentences.zh: 史官當會集日月之行，以求合朔。

translations.literal: Historians ought to gather the motions of sun and moon to seek conjunction at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers must combine the motions of sun and moon to find true conjunction.

sentences.zh: 自漢太初至於今，冬至差十日，如劉歆《三統》復強于古，故先儒謂之最疏。

translations.literal: From Han Taichu to the present, the winter solstice has differed by ten days; as Liu Xin's Triple Concordance was again stronger than the ancients', former scholars called it the loosest.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han Taichu era to the present, winter solstice has drifted by ten days. Liu Xin's Triple Concordance was even more forced than antiquity, so earlier scholars called it the least accurate.

sentences.zh: 後漢劉洪考驗《四分》，於天不合，乃減朔余，苟合時用。

translations.literal: Later Han Liu Hong verified the Quarter-Remainder against heaven and found it did not match, so he reduced the new-moon remainder to suit current use.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Liu Hong tested the Quarter-Remainder Calendar against the heavens, found it wanting, and reduced the new-moon remainder to fit contemporary practice.

sentences.zh: 自是已降，率意加減，以造日法。

translations.literal: From then downward, they arbitrarily added and subtracted to make day divisors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter calendar-makers arbitrarily adjusted figures to derive new day divisors.

sentences.zh: 宋世何承天更以四十九分之二十六為強率，十七分之九為弱率，於強弱之際以求日法。

translations.literal: In Song times He Chengtian further took 26/49 as the strong rate and 9/17 as the weak rate, seeking the day divisor at the juncture of strong and weak.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liu Song, He Chengtian used 26/49 as the "strong" rate and 9/17 as the "weak" rate, seeking the day divisor between them.

sentences.zh: 承天日法七百五十二，得一十五強一弱。

translations.literal: He Chengtian's day divisor was 752, yielding fifteen strong and one weak.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's day divisor was 752, equivalent to fifteen strong units and one weak.

sentences.zh: 自後治曆者，莫不因承天法、累強弱之數，皆不悟日月有自然合會之數。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers afterward all followed He Chengtian's method, piling strong-and-weak numbers, yet none grasped that sun and moon have a natural number of conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Later calendar-makers all followed He Chengtian's strong-and-weak method without realizing that sun and moon possess a natural number of conjunction.

sentences.zh: 今稍悟其失，定新曆以三萬九千為日法，六百二十四萬為度母，九千五百為鬥分，二萬六百九十三為朔餘，可以上稽于古，下驗於今，反覆推求，若應繩准。

translations.literal: Now having slightly grasped this failure, we fix the new calendar with thirty-nine thousand as day divisor, six million two hundred forty thousand as degree mother, nine thousand five hundred as Dipper fraction, twenty thousand six hundred ninety-three as new-moon remainder, so that it can be checked against antiquity above and verified in the present below; pursued back and forth, it answers like a plumb line.
translations.idiomatic: Having discerned this flaw, the new calendar sets the day divisor at 39,000, the degree mother at 6,240,000, the Dipper fraction at 9,500, and the new-moon remainder at 20,693—checking against antiquity above and the present below, repeated inquiry shows it true as a plumb line.

sentences.zh: 又以二百三十萬一千為月行之餘，月行十三度之餘。

translations.literal: Further, two million three hundred one thousand is taken as the moon's motion remainder, the remainder of the moon's thirteen-degree motion.
translations.idiomatic: Further, 2,301,000 is set as the remainder of the moon's motion—the fractional part of its 13° motion.

sentences.zh: 以一百六十萬四百四十七為日行之餘。

translations.literal: One million six hundred thousand four hundred forty-seven is taken as the sun's motion remainder.
translations.idiomatic: 1,600,447 is set as the remainder of the sun's motion.

sentences.zh: 日行周天之餘。

translations.literal: The remainder of the sun's daily circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fractional remainder of the sun's daily circuit.

sentences.zh: 乃會日月之行，以盈不足平之，並盈不足，是為一朔之法。

translations.literal: Then combining sun and moon's motions, leveling excess and deficit, and joining excess with deficit—this is the method for one new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Combining the sun's and moon's motions, excess and deficit are balanced and joined; this yields the method for one new moon.

sentences.zh: 日法也，名元法。

translations.literal: It is the day divisor, also called the origin divisor.
translations.idiomatic: This is the day divisor, also termed the origin divisor.

sentences.zh: 今乃以大月乘不足之數，以小月乘盈行之分，平而並之，是為一朔之實。

translations.literal: Now the long month multiplies the deficit number, the short month multiplies the excess parts; leveled and joined, this is the full measure of one new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The long month multiplies the deficit figure and the short month the excess parts; averaged and combined, this gives the true value of one new moon.

sentences.zh: 周天分也。

translations.literal: It is the circuit-of-heaven parts.
translations.idiomatic: This is the circuit-of-heaven fraction.

sentences.zh: 以法約實，得日月相會之數，皆以等數約之，悉得今有之數。

translations.literal: Using the divisor to reduce the full measure, one obtains the number of sun-and-moon conjunction; all are reduced by equal divisors to obtain entirely the numbers now at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing the true value by the divisor yields the conjunction number; reducing by common divisors produces exactly the figures used today.

sentences.zh: 盈為朔虛，不足為朔餘。

translations.literal: Excess becomes new-moon void, deficit becomes new-moon remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Excess becomes the new-moon void fraction; deficit becomes the new-moon remainder.

sentences.zh: 又二法相乘為本母，各母互乘，以減周天，餘則歲差生焉，亦以等數約之，即得歲差、度母、周天實用之數。

translations.literal: Further, multiplying the two divisors makes the fundamental mother; each mother multiplies the other, subtract from the circuit of heaven, and the remainder yields the annual difference; also reduced by equal divisors, one obtains the annual difference, degree mother, and circuit-of-heaven numbers in practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying the two divisors gives the fundamental mother; cross-multiplying and subtracting from the circuit of heaven yields the precession remainder, which common reduction converts to the precession, degree mother, and practical circuit-of-heaven values.

sentences.zh: 此之一法，理極幽眇，所謂反覆相求，潛遁相通，數有冥符，法有偶會，古曆家皆所未達。

translations.literal: This single method is most subtle in principle—what is called seeking back and forth, secretly passing and connecting; numbers have hidden correspondence, methods have chance pairing—none of the ancient calendar-makers reached it.
translations.idiomatic: This method is profoundly subtle: repeated mutual calculation, hidden interconnection, numbers in secret correspondence, methods in felicitous alignment—none of the ancient calendar-makers had attained it.

sentences.zh: 以等數約之，得三萬九千為元法，九千五百為鬥分，二萬六百九十三為朔餘，六百二十四萬為日度母，二十二億七千九百二十萬四百四十七為周天分，八萬四百四十七為歲差。

translations.literal: Reduced by equal divisors, thirty-nine thousand becomes the origin divisor, nine thousand five hundred the Dipper fraction, twenty thousand six hundred ninety-three the new-moon remainder, six million two hundred forty thousand the day-degree mother, two billion two hundred seventy-nine million two hundred thousand four hundred forty-seven the circuit-of-heaven parts, and eighty thousand four hundred forty-seven the annual difference.
translations.idiomatic: Common reduction yields 39,000 as the origin divisor, 9,500 as the Dipper fraction, 20,693 as the new-moon remainder, 6,240,000 as the day-degree mother, 2,279,200,447 as the circuit-of-heaven parts, and 80,447 as the precession value.

sentences.zh: 歲餘：九千五百。

translations.literal: Annual remainder: nine thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Annual remainder: 9,500.

sentences.zh: 古曆曰鬥分。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars call it the Dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars termed this the Dipper fraction.

sentences.zh: 古者以周天三百六十五度四分度之一，是為鬥分。

translations.literal: Antiquity took the circuit of heaven as three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees—this is the Dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity defined the circuit of heaven as 365¼ degrees—the Dipper fraction.

sentences.zh: 夫舉正於中，上稽往古，下驗當時，反覆參求，合符應准，然後施行於百代，為不易之術。

translations.literal: To take the mean as correct, check antiquity above and the present below, compare back and forth until signs match the standard, then implement through a hundred generations as an unchanging technique.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the mean as standard, checking past and present, comparing until all accord—only then may it serve for generations as an unchanging method.

sentences.zh: 自後治曆者，測今冬至日晷，用校古法，過盈，以萬為母，課諸氣分，率二千五百以下、二千四百二十八已上為中平之率。

translations.literal: Calendar-makers afterward measured the winter-solstice gnomon shadow of the day, used it to check ancient methods—finding excess, took ten thousand as mother, tested against qi divisions, taking rates below 2500 and from 2428 upward as the mean rate.
translations.idiomatic: Later makers measured contemporary winter-solstice shadows, compared them to antique methods, and when excess appeared used 10,000 as denominator; qi-period tests showed rates between 2428 and 2500 as the mean.

sentences.zh: 新曆鬥分九千五百，以萬平之，得二千四百二十五半盈，得中平之數也。

translations.literal: The new calendar's Dipper fraction nine thousand five hundred, leveled by ten thousand, yields two thousand four hundred twenty-five and a half excess, obtaining the mean number.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar's Dipper fraction of 9,500, normalized to 10,000, gives 2,425.5 excess—the mean figure.

sentences.zh: 而三萬九千年冬至小余成九千五百日，滿朔實一百一十五萬一千六百九十三，年齊於日分，而氣朔相會。

translations.literal: And in thirty-nine thousand years the winter-solstice small remainder becomes nine thousand five hundred days; filling the new-moon full measure of one million one hundred fifty-one thousand six hundred ninety-three, the year's length aligns with the day fraction, and qi and new moon meet.
translations.idiomatic: Over 39,000 years the winter-solstice small remainder accrues to 9,500 days; filling the new-moon true value of 1,151,693 aligns the year with the day fraction so qi and new moon coincide.

sentences.zh: 歲周：一千四百二十四萬四千五百。

translations.literal: Annual circuit: fourteen million two hundred forty-four thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Annual circuit: 14,244,500.

sentences.zh: 以元法乘三百六十五度，內鬥分九千五百，得之，即為一歲之日分，故曰歲周。

translations.literal: Multiplying the origin divisor by 365 degrees, adding within the Dipper fraction 9500, obtaining this—this is one year's day-parts, hence called annual circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying the origin divisor by 365° and adding the Dipper fraction 9,500 gives one year's day-parts—the annual circuit.

sentences.zh: 若以二十四均之，得一十五日、餘八千五百二十、秒一十五，為一氣之策也。

translations.literal: If divided by twenty-four, one obtains fifteen days, remainder 8520, seconds 15—this is one qi cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Divided by 24, this yields 15 days, 8,520 parts, and 15 seconds per qi period.

sentences.zh: 朔實：一百一十五萬一千六百九十三。

translations.literal: New-moon full measure: one million one hundred fifty-one thousand six hundred ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: New-moon true value: 1,151,693.

sentences.zh: 本會日月之行，以盈不足平而得二萬六百九十三，是為朔餘，備在調日法術中。

translations.literal: Originally combining sun and moon's motions, leveling excess and deficit to obtain twenty thousand six hundred ninety-three—this is the new-moon remainder, fully set forth in the method for adjusting the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Combining the sun's and moon's motions and balancing excess and deficit yields 20,693 as the new-moon remainder, as detailed in the day-divisor adjustment method.

sentences.zh: 是則四象全策之餘也。

translations.literal: This is then the remainder of the four phases' full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: This is the remainder of the full four-phase cycle.

sentences.zh: 今以元法乘四象全策二十九，總而並之，是為一朔之實也。

translations.literal: Now multiplying the origin divisor by the four phases' full cycle of twenty-nine, totaling and joining them—this is the full measure of one new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying the origin divisor by the four-phase full cycle of 29 and summing them gives the true value of one new moon.

sentences.zh: 古曆以一百萬平朔餘之分，得五十三萬六百以下、五百七十已上，是為中平之率。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars leveled new-moon remainder parts by one million, obtaining below 530,600 and from 570 upward as the mean rate.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars normalized new-moon remainder parts to 1,000,000, taking figures below 530,600 and from 570 upward as the mean rate.

sentences.zh: 新曆以一百萬平之，得五十三萬五百八十九，得中平之數也。

translations.literal: The new calendar, leveled by one million, yields five hundred thirty thousand five hundred eighty-nine, obtaining the mean number.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar, normalized to 1,000,000, gives 530,589—the mean figure.

sentences.zh: 若以四象均之，得七日，余一萬四千九百二十三、秒，是為弦策也。

translations.literal: If divided by the four phases, one obtains seven days, remainder fourteen thousand nine hundred twenty-three and seconds—this is the quarter-moon cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Divided by four phases, this yields 7 days, 14,923 parts, and seconds—the quarter-moon cycle.

sentences.zh: 中盈、朔虛分：閏餘附

translations.literal: Mid-qi excess and new-moon void fractions: appendix on intercalary remainder
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Qi Excess and New-Moon Void Fractions: Appendix on Intercalary Remainder

sentences.zh: 日月以會朔為正，氣序以鬥建為中，是故氣進而盈分存焉。

translations.literal: Sun and moon take conjunction at new moon as correct; the qi sequence takes the Dipper's establishment as center—hence as qi advances, excess parts remain.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon take conjunction at new moon as the standard; the qi sequence takes the Dipper's establishment as the center—thus as qi advances, excess parts accumulate.

sentences.zh: 置中節兩氣之策，以一月之全策三十減之，每至中氣，即一萬七千四十、秒十二，是為中盈分。

translations.literal: Set the two qi cycles of the mid-season node, subtract from the month's full cycle of thirty; at each mid-qi, it is seventeen thousand forty, seconds twelve—this is the mid-qi excess fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the two qi cycles of the mid-season node and subtracting from the month's full cycle of 30, each mid-qi yields 17,040 parts and 12 seconds—the mid-qi excess fraction.

sentences.zh: 朔退而虛分列焉，置一月之全策三十，以朔策及餘減之，余一萬八千三百七，是為朔虛分。

translations.literal: As new moon retreats, void fractions are listed; set the month's full cycle of thirty, subtract the new-moon cycle and remainder—remainder eighteen thousand three hundred seven—this is the new-moon void fraction.
translations.idiomatic: As new moon retreats, void fractions appear: subtract the new-moon cycle and remainder from the month's full cycle of 30; the remainder 18,307 is the new-moon void fraction.

sentences.zh: 綜中盈、朔虛分，而閏余章焉。

translations.literal: Combining mid-qi excess and new-moon void fractions, the intercalary remainder chapter is formed.
translations.idiomatic: Combining mid-qi excess and new-moon void fractions yields the intercalary remainder chapter.

sentences.zh: 閏余三萬五千三百四十五、秒一十三。

translations.literal: Intercalary remainder: thirty-five thousand three hundred forty-five, seconds thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary remainder: 35,345, seconds 13.

sentences.zh: 從消息而自致，以盈虛名焉。

translations.literal: Following waxing and waning it comes of itself, named by excess and void.
translations.idiomatic: It arises naturally from waxing and waning, and is named for excess and void.

sentences.zh: 紀法：六十。

translations.literal: Cycle divisor: sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Cycle divisor: 60.

sentences.zh: 《易·乾》象之爻九，《坤》象之爻六，《震》、《坎》、《艮》象之爻皆七，《巽》、《離》、《兌》象之爻皆八。

translations.literal: In the Changes, Qian's image has nine lines, Kun's six; Zhen, Kan, and Gen each have seven; Xun, Li, and Dui each have eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes, the Qian trigram has nine lines, Kun six; Zhen, Kan, and Gen each seven; Xun, Li, and Dui each eight.

sentences.zh: 綜八卦之數凡六十，又六旬之數也。

translations.literal: Summing the eight trigrams' numbers totals sixty—also the number of a six-decade cycle.
translations.idiomatic: The eight trigrams' line-counts sum to 60—the same as a sexagenary cycle.

sentences.zh: 紀者，終也，數終八卦，故以紀名焉。

translations.literal: Cycle means end; the numbers end with the eight trigrams, hence the name cycle.
translations.idiomatic: A cycle (ji) means an end; the count completes the eight trigrams, hence the name.

sentences.zh: 天正冬至：大余五十七，小余一萬七千。

translations.literal: Heaven's first month, winter solstice: large remainder fifty-seven, small remainder seventeen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's first month, winter solstice: large remainder 57, small remainder 17,000.

sentences.zh: 先測立冬晷景，次取測立春晷景，取近者通計，半之，為距至泛日；

translations.literal: First measure the Beginning-of-Winter gnomon shadow, next measure the Beginning-of-Spring shadow; take the nearer, compute through, halve it—this is the general day-distance to the solstice;
translations.idiomatic: First measure the Beginning-of-Winter gnomon shadow, then the Beginning-of-Spring shadow; take the nearer, compute through, and halve it to get the approximate day-distance to the solstice;

sentences.zh: 乃以晷數相減，餘者以法乘之，滿其日晷差而一，為差刻；

translations.literal: then subtract the gnomon numbers; the remainder multiplied by the divisor, divided by the daily gnomon difference, yields one—this is the difference in clepsydra marks;
translations.idiomatic: subtract the shadow lengths; multiply the remainder by the divisor and divide by the daily shadow difference to obtain the correction in clepsydra marks;

sentences.zh: 乃以差刻求冬至，視其前晷多則為減，少則為加，求夏至者反之。

translations.literal: then use the difference marks to seek winter solstice—if the prior shadow is greater, subtract; if less, add; for summer solstice, reverse.
translations.idiomatic: then apply the correction marks to find winter solstice: if the prior shadow is longer, subtract; if shorter, add; reverse the procedure for summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 加減距至泛日，為定日；

translations.literal: adding or subtracting from the general day-distance to the solstice gives the fixed day;
translations.idiomatic: Adding or subtracting from the approximate day-distance yields the fixed date;

sentences.zh: 仍加半日之刻，命從前距日辰，算外，即二至加時日辰及刻分所在。

translations.literal: still add half a day's marks, count from the prior day's distance hour, outside the count—this is the day, hour, and mark-fraction of the solstice's added time.
translations.idiomatic: add half a day's clepsydra marks, count from the prior day's distance hour, and the result gives the day, hour, and marks of true solstice time.

sentences.zh: 如此推求，則加時與日晷相協。

translations.literal: Pursued thus, the added time agrees with the gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated thus, true time agrees with the gnomon shadow.

sentences.zh: 今須積歲四百一年，治平元年甲辰歲，氣積年也。

translations.literal: Now one must accumulate four hundred one years; the first year of Zhiping, year jiachen, is the accumulated qi years.
translations.idiomatic: The accumulated count must be 401 years; the first year of Zhiping (1064), year jiachen, is the accumulated qi epoch.

sentences.zh: 則冬至大、小餘與今適會。

translations.literal: Then the winter solstice's large and small remainders meet the present exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Then the winter solstice large and small remainders match the present exactly.

sentences.zh: 天正經朔：大余三十四，小余三萬一千。

translations.literal: Heaven's first month, standard new moon: large remainder thirty-four, small remainder thirty-one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's first month, standard new moon: large remainder 34, small remainder 31,000.

sentences.zh: 閏余八十八萬三千九百九十。

translations.literal: Intercalary remainder: eight hundred eighty-three thousand nine hundred ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary remainder: 883,990.

sentences.zh: 則經朔大、小餘與今有之數，偕閏余而相會。

translations.literal: Then the standard new moon's large and small remainders, with the numbers now at hand, meet together with the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Then the standard new moon's large and small remainders, together with the intercalary remainder, coincide with present figures.

sentences.zh: 日度歲差：八萬四百四十七。

translations.literal: Day-degree annual difference: eighty thousand four hundred forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Day-degree precession: 80,447.

sentences.zh: 《書》舉正南之星以正四方，蓋先王以明時授人，奉天育物。

translations.literal: The Documents cites the star due south to rectify the four directions—for the ancient kings used clear seasons to instruct the people, serving Heaven and nurturing things.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents cites the star due south to orient the four directions, for the ancient kings used the seasons to instruct the people, serving Heaven and nurturing all things.

sentences.zh: 然先儒所述，互有同異。

translations.literal: Yet what former scholars described mutually differed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet earlier scholars' accounts differ among themselves.

sentences.zh: 虞喜云：「堯時冬至日短星昴，今二千七百餘年，乃東壁中，則知每歲漸差之所至。」

translations.literal: Yu Xi said: "At Yao's time, at winter solstice the day was short and the star was Mao; now after more than twenty-seven hundred years it is at the center of Eastern Wall—thus one knows where the annual gradual difference reaches."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi said: "At Yao's time, winter solstice fell when the day was short and Mao was culminating; after more than 2,700 years it is at the center of Eastern Wall—thus we know the extent of the annual drift."

sentences.zh: 又何承天云：「《堯典》：'日永星火，以正仲夏；

translations.literal: He Chengtian also said: "The Canon of Yao: 'The day is longest and the Fire star is bright, to rectify midsummer;
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian also said: "The Canon of Yao reads: 'The day is longest and the Fire star is bright, to mark midsummer;

sentences.zh: 宵中星虛，以正仲秋。

translations.literal: the night is centered and the star is Xu, to rectify mid-autumn.
translations.idiomatic: the night is centered and Xu is culminating, to mark mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: '今以中星校之，所差二十七八度，即堯時冬至，日在須女十度。」

translations.literal: Now checking by the culminating star, the difference is twenty-seven or eight degrees—thus at Yao's winter solstice the sun was at Woman, ten degrees."
translations.idiomatic: Checking by the culminating stars today, the difference is 27 or 28 degrees—at Yao's winter solstice the sun stood at Woman, 10°."

sentences.zh: 故祖沖之修《大明曆》，始立歲差，率四十五年九月卻一度。

translations.literal: Hence Zu Chongzhi, revising the Great Enlightenment Calendar, first established annual difference, at the rate of one degree retreating in forty-five years nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zu Chongzhi, revising the Daming Calendar, first established precession at the rate of one degree every 45 years and 9 months.

sentences.zh: 虞鄺、劉孝孫等因之，各有增損，以創新法。

translations.literal: Yu Kui, Liu Xiaosun, and others followed, each adding or subtracting to create new methods.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kui, Liu Xiaosun, and others followed suit, each adjusting the rate to devise new methods.

sentences.zh: 若從虞喜之驗，昴中則五十餘年日退一度；

translations.literal: If following Yu Xi's verification, with Mao at center the sun retreats one degree in fifty-odd years;
translations.idiomatic: By Yu Xi's verification, with Mao at culmination the sun retreats one degree in just over 50 years;

sentences.zh: 若依承天之驗，火中又不及百年日退一度。

translations.literal: if following He Chengtian's verification, with Fire at center not even a hundred years before the sun retreats one degree.
translations.idiomatic: by He Chengtian's verification, with Fire at culmination the sun retreats one degree in less than a century.

sentences.zh: 後《皇極》綜兩曆之率而要取其中，故七十五年而退一度，此乃通其意未盡其微。

translations.literal: Later the Imperial Ultimate synthesized the two calendars' rates and took the mean, hence seventy-five years to retreat one degree—this grasped the idea but did not exhaust the subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Huangji Calendar averaged the two rates, yielding one degree every 75 years—this captured the idea but not the full subtlety.

sentences.zh: 今則別調新率，改立歲差，大率七十七年七月，日退一度，上元命於虛九，可以上覆往古，下逮於今。

translations.literal: Now we separately adjust a new rate, reform and establish annual difference—on the whole seventy-seven years seven months for the sun to retreat one degree; the upper origin is fixed at Void nine, able to cover antiquity above and reach to the present below.
translations.idiomatic: Now a new rate is set and precession re-established at roughly one degree every 77 years and 7 months; the upper origin is fixed at Void 9°, covering antiquity above and the present below.

sentences.zh: 自帝堯以來，迴圈考驗，新曆歲差，皆得其中，最為親近。

translations.literal: From Emperor Yao downward, tested in cycles round and round, the new calendar's annual difference all hits the mean—most closely approximate.
translations.idiomatic: Tested cyclically from Emperor Yao to the present, the new calendar's precession hits the mean most closely.

sentences.zh: 周天分：二十二億七千九百二十萬四百四十七。

translations.literal: Circuit-of-heaven parts: two billion two hundred seventy-nine million two hundred thousand four hundred forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit-of-heaven parts: 2,279,200,447.

sentences.zh: 本齊日月之行，會合朔而得之。

translations.literal: Originally aligning sun and moon's motions, obtained by meeting at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Derived by aligning the sun's and moon's motions at conjunction at new moon.

sentences.zh: 在調日法。

translations.literal: It is in the method for adjusting the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: See the day-divisor adjustment method.

sentences.zh: 使上考仲康房、宿之交，下驗薑岌月食之沖，三十年間，若應準繩，則新曆周天，有自然冥符之數，最為密近。

translations.literal: Let it be checked above at Zhongkang's crossing of Room and Lodging, verified below at Jiang Kui's lunar eclipse opposition—within thirty years, if it answers like a plumb line, then the new calendar's circuit of heaven has a natural hidden-correspondence number, most closely dense.
translations.idiomatic: Checking above at Zhong Kang's Room-Lodging crossing and below at Jiang Kui's lunar eclipse, over thirty years if all matches like a plumb line, the new calendar's circuit of heaven has a naturally corresponding number—most precise of all.

sentences.zh: 日躔盈縮定差：張胄玄名損益率曰盈縮數，劉孝孫以盈縮數為朏朒積，《皇極》有陟降率、遲疾數，《麟德》曰先後、盈縮數，《大衍》曰損益、朏朒積，《崇天》曰損益、盈縮積。

translations.literal: Solar lodge excess-deficit fixed difference: Zhang Zhouxuan named the increase-decrease rate the excess-deficit number; Liu Xiaosun took the excess-deficit number as the crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Imperial Ultimate had ascent-descent rate and slow-fast number; the Qilin Virtue called them before-after and excess-deficit number; the Great Expansion increase-decrease and crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Honoring Heaven increase-decrease and excess-deficit accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Solar motion excess-deficit fixed difference: Zhang Zhouxuan called the increase-decrease rate the excess-deficit number; Liu Xiaosun termed it the crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Huangji had ascent-descent rate and slow-fast number; the Lindé calendar used before-after and excess-deficit number; the Dayan used increase-decrease and crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Chongtian used increase-decrease and excess-deficit accumulation.

sentences.zh: 所謂古曆平朔之日，而月或朝覿東方，夕見西方，則史官謂之朏朒。

translations.literal: What is called the ancient calendar's mean-new-moon day—yet the moon might be seen in the east at dawn and in the west at dusk—historians called this crescent-gibbous.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient mean-new-moon calendars could show the moon visible in the east at dawn and in the west at dusk on the same day—astronomers called this a crescent-gibbous anomaly.

sentences.zh: 今以日行之所盈縮、月行之所遲疾，皆損益之，或進退其日，以為定朔，則舒亟之度，乃勢數使然，非失政之致也。

translations.literal: Now taking the sun's motion excess-deficit and moon's motion slow-fast, all are increased or decreased, sometimes advancing or retreating the day, to make fixed new moon—then the degrees of slack and urgency are the tendency of numbers, not caused by misgovernment.
translations.idiomatic: Now adjusting for the sun's excess-deficit and the moon's slow-fast motion, advancing or retreating the day to obtain true new moon—the varying pace follows numerical necessity, not governmental failure.

sentences.zh: 新曆以七千一為盈縮之極，其數與月離相錯，而損益、盈縮為名，則文約而義見。

translations.literal: The new calendar takes seven thousand one as the pole of excess-deficit; its number crosses with lunar departure, yet naming increase-decrease and excess-deficit, the text is concise and the meaning clear.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar sets 7,001 as the maximum excess-deficit; its figure interlocks with lunar motion, and naming them increase-decrease and excess-deficit keeps the text concise yet clear.

sentences.zh: 升降分：《皇極》躔衰有陟降率，《麟德》以日景差、陟降率、日晷景消息為之，義通軌漏。

translations.literal: Ascent-descent fraction: the Imperial Ultimate's lodge decline had ascent-descent rate; the Qilin Virtue used daily shadow difference, ascent-descent rate, and gnomon shadow waxing-waning—the meaning connects with clepsydra tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent-descent fraction: the Huangji calendar's lodge decline used an ascent-descent rate; the Lindé used daily shadow difference, ascent-descent rate, and gnomon shadow waxing-waning—equivalent to clepsydra regulation.

sentences.zh: 夫南至之後，日行漸升，去極近，故晷短而萬物皆盛；

translations.literal: After the southern extreme, the sun's path gradually rises, near the pole—hence shadows are short and all things flourish;
translations.idiomatic: After the southern solstice, the sun's path gradually rises toward the pole, shadows shorten, and all things flourish;

sentences.zh: 北至之後，日行漸降，去極遠，故晷長而萬物浸衰。

translations.literal: after the northern extreme, the sun's path gradually descends, far from the pole—hence shadows are long and all things gradually decline.
translations.idiomatic: after the northern solstice, the sun's path gradually descends from the pole, shadows lengthen, and all things gradually decline.

sentences.zh: 自《大衍》以下，皆從《麟德》。

translations.literal: From the Great Expansion downward, all followed the Qilin Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dayan calendar onward, all followed the Lindé method.

sentences.zh: 今曆消息日行之升降，積而為盈縮焉。

translations.literal: The present calendar tracks the sun's path waxing and waning, accumulating into excess-deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar tracks the sun's waxing and waning motion, accumulating it into excess-deficit.

sentences.zh: 赤道宿：漢百二年議造曆，乃定東西，立晷儀，下漏刻，以追二十八宿相距于四方，赤道宿度，則其法也。

translations.literal: Equatorial lodges: in Han year 102 they debated making a calendar, fixed east and west, set up the gnomon instrument, lowered clepsydra marks, to pursue the twenty-eight lodges' distances in the four directions—equatorial lodge degrees were that method.
translations.idiomatic: Equatorial lodges: in 99 BCE the court debated calendar reform, fixed east and west, erected the gnomon, set clepsydra marks, and measured the twenty-eight lodges' spacing in the four directions—equatorial lodge degrees were the method.

sentences.zh: 其赤道，鬥二十六度及分，牛八度，女十二度，虛十度，危十七度，室十六度，壁九度，奎十六度，婁十二度，胃十四度，昴十一度，畢十六度，觜二度，參九度，井三十三度，鬼四度，柳十五度，星七度，張十八度，翼十八度，軫十七度，角十二度，亢九度，氐十五度，房五度，心五度，尾十八度，箕十一度，自後相承用之。

translations.literal: Its equator: Dipper 26 degrees and fraction, Ox 8, Woman 12, Void 10, Rooftop 17, Encampment 16, Wall 9, Stride 16, Bond 12, Stomach 14, Hairy Head 11, Net 16, Turtle Beak 2, Three Stars 9, Well 33, Ghost 4, Willow 15, Star 7, Extended Net 18, Wings 18, Chariot Shaft 17, Horn 12, Gullet 9, Base 15, Room 5, Heart 5, Tail 18, Winnowing Basket 11—used in succession thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Its equatorial degrees: Dipper 26°+, Ox 8°, Woman 12°, Void 10°, Rooftop 17°, Encampment 16°, Wall 9°, Stride 16°, Bond 12°, Stomach 14°, Hairy Head 11°, Net 16°, Turtle Beak 2°, Three Stars 9°, Well 33°, Ghost 4°, Willow 15°, Star 7°, Extended Net 18°, Wings 18°, Chariot Shaft 17°, Horn 12°, Gullet 9°, Base 15°, Room 5°, Heart 5°, Tail 18°, Winnowing Basket 11°—used in succession thereafter.

sentences.zh: 至唐初，李淳風造渾儀，亦無所改。

translations.literal: By early Tang, Li Chunfeng made the armillary sphere, also changing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, Li Chunfeng built the armillary sphere without altering these figures.

sentences.zh: 開元中，浮屠一行作《大衍曆》，詔梁令瓚作黃道遊儀，測知畢、觜、參及輿鬼四宿赤道宿度，與舊不同。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, the monk Yixing made the Great Expansion Calendar; an edict ordered Liang Lingzan to make the ecliptic touring instrument, measuring Net, Turtle Beak, Three Stars, and Ghost-Cart's four lodges' equatorial degrees—differing from the old.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, the monk Yixing compiled the Dayan Calendar; Liang Lingzan was ordered to build the ecliptic touring instrument and found the equatorial degrees of Net, Turtle Beak, Three Stars, and Ghost differed from the old values.

sentences.zh: 畢十七度，觜一度，參十度，鬼三度。

translations.literal: Net seventeen degrees, Turtle Beak one degree, Three Stars ten degrees, Ghost three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Net 17°, Turtle Beak 1°, Three Stars 10°, Ghost 3°.

sentences.zh: 自一行之後，因相沿襲，下更五代，無所增損。

translations.literal: From after Yixing, following in succession, down through five dynasties, nothing was added or subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: After Yixing, the values were passed down unchanged through five dynasties.

sentences.zh: 至仁宗皇祐初，始有詔造黃道渾儀，鑄銅為之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Renzong's Huangyou era, there was first an edict to make an ecliptic armillary sphere, casting it in bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Renzong's Huangyou reign, an edict ordered a bronze ecliptic armillary sphere to be cast.

sentences.zh: 自後測驗赤道宿度，又一十四宿與一行所測不同。

translations.literal: Thereafter testing equatorial lodge degrees, again fourteen lodges differed from what Yixing measured.
translations.idiomatic: Later measurements found fourteen more lodges whose equatorial degrees differed from Yixing's values.

sentences.zh: 鬥二十五度，牛七度，女十一度，危十六度，室十七度，胃十五度，畢十八度，井三十四度，鬼二度，柳十四度，氐十六度，心六度，尾十九度，箕十度。

translations.literal: Dipper twenty-five degrees, Ox seven degrees, Woman eleven degrees, Rooftop sixteen degrees, Encampment seventeen degrees, Stomach fifteen degrees, Net eighteen degrees, Well thirty-four degrees, Ghost two degrees, Willow fourteen degrees, Base sixteen degrees, Heart six degrees, Tail nineteen degrees, Winnowing Basket ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper 25°, Ox 7°, Woman 11°, Rooftop 16°, Encampment 17°, Stomach 15°, Net 18°, Well 34°, Ghost 2°, Willow 14°, Base 16°, Heart 6°, Tail 19°, Winnowing Basket 10°.

sentences.zh: 蓋古今之人，以八尺圓器，欲以盡天體，決知其難矣。

translations.literal: For ancient and modern men alike, using an eight-foot circular instrument to try to exhaust the celestial body—surely knowing this is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern observers alike have known that an eight-foot circular instrument cannot fully compass the heavens.

sentences.zh: 又況圖本所指距星，傳習有差，故今赤道宿度與古不同。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reference stars indicated in diagrams, handed down with discrepancies—hence today's equatorial lodge degrees differ from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, reference stars in inherited star charts vary, so present equatorial degrees differ from ancient ones.

sentences.zh: 自漢太初後至唐開元治曆之初，凡八百年間，悉無更易。

translations.literal: From after Han Taichu to the beginning of Tang Kaiyuan's calendar-making, altogether eight hundred years, entirely without change.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han Taichu calendar through the start of Tang Kaiyuan calendar reform—some eight hundred years—there had been no revisions.

sentences.zh: 今雖測驗與舊不同，亦歲月未久。

translations.literal: Though today's testing differs from the old, the years and months are not yet long.
translations.idiomatic: Though recent measurements differ from older values, not much time has passed.

sentences.zh: 新曆兩備其數，如淳風從舊之意。

translations.literal: The new calendar keeps both sets of numbers, as Li Chunfeng's intent to follow the old.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar retains both sets of figures, in the spirit of Li Chunfeng's adherence to tradition.

sentences.zh: 月度轉分：《洪範傳》曰：「晦而月見西方謂之朏。

translations.literal: Monthly degree rotation fraction: the Commentary on the Hong Fan says: "At the last day of the month, the moon seen in the west is called fei (incipient crescent).
translations.idiomatic: Monthly rotation fraction: the Commentary on the Hong Fan states: "When the moon is seen in the west on the last day of the month, it is called fei (incipient crescent).

sentences.zh: 月未合朔，在日後；

translations.literal: The moon has not yet conjoined at new moon—it is behind the sun;
translations.idiomatic: The moon has not yet reached conjunction at new moon and still lags behind the sun;

sentences.zh: 今在日前，太疾也。

translations.literal: now it is before the sun—too fast.
translations.idiomatic: now it stands before the sun—too fast.

sentences.zh: 朏者，人君舒緩、臣下驕盈專權之象。

translations.literal: Fei is the image of the lord easing and slackening, ministers arrogant, swollen, and monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: An incipient crescent signaled a lax sovereign and arrogant, overbearing ministers.

sentences.zh: 朔而月見東方謂之側匿。

translations.literal: At new moon, the moon seen in the east is called ce ni (hiding aside).
translations.idiomatic: If the moon appears in the east at new moon, it is called ce ni (hiding aside).

sentences.zh: 合朔則月與日合，今在日後，太遲也。

translations.literal: At conjunction new moon the moon and sun unite; now behind the sun—too slow.
translations.idiomatic: At true new moon sun and moon conjoin; if the moon still lags behind the sun, it is too slow.

sentences.zh: 側匿者，人君嚴急、臣下危殆恐懼之象。」

translations.literal: Ce ni is the image of the lord strict and urgent, ministers endangered and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Ce ni betokened a stern sovereign and ministers in peril and dread."

sentences.zh: 盈則進，縮則退，躔離九道，周合三旬，考其變行，自有常數。

translations.literal: When full then advance, when shrunken then retreat; lodges depart the nine paths, cycle joining three ten-day weeks—investigating its changing motion, there are of themselves constant numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When full it advances, when shrunken it retreats; the moon traverses and leaves the nine paths, completing a cycle in thirty days—investigate its changing motion and fixed numbers appear."

sentences.zh: 《傳》稱，人君有舒疾之變，未達月有遲速之常也。

translations.literal: The Commentary says that when the lord has slack-urgent changes, one has not yet grasped that the moon has slow-fast constants.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary warns that attributing slackness or urgency to the sovereign misses the moon's regular alternation of slow and fast motion.

sentences.zh: 後漢劉洪粗通其旨。

translations.literal: Later Han's Liu Hong roughly grasped its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong of Later Han grasped the principle in outline.

sentences.zh: 爾後治曆者多循舊法，皆考遲疾之分，增損平會之朔，得月後定追及日之際而生定朔焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter calendar-makers mostly followed old methods, all examining slow-fast divisions, increasing and decreasing mean-conjunction new moons, obtaining when the moon fixedly catches up to the sun to produce fixed new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Later calendar-makers mostly followed older methods, reckoning slow-fast divisions and adjusting mean conjunctions until the moon's fixed catch-up with the sun yielded true new moon.

sentences.zh: 至於加時早晚，或速或遲，皆由轉分強弱所致。

translations.literal: As for the time of addition early or late, sometimes fast sometimes slow—all caused by rotation fraction strong-weak.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the computed hour came early or late, fast or slow, all stemmed from the strength or weakness of the rotation fraction.

sentences.zh: 舊曆課轉分，以九分之五為強率，一百一分之五十六為弱率，乃於強弱之際而求秒焉。

translations.literal: The old calendar tabulated rotation fraction, taking five-ninths as strong rate, fifty-six one-hundred-and-firsts as weak rate, then at the border of strong and weak seeking seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendar computed rotation fractions with a strong rate of 5/9 and a weak rate of 56/101, deriving seconds at the transition between them.

sentences.zh: 新曆轉分二百九十八億八千二百二十四萬二千二百五十一，以一百萬平之，得二十七日五十五萬四千六百二十六，最得中平之數。

translations.literal: The new calendar's rotation fraction: 29,882,422,251; averaged by one million, obtaining 27 days 554,626—most attaining the mean-even number.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar's rotation fraction is 29,882,422,251; divided by 1,000,000 this yields 27 days 554,626—the most balanced mean value.

sentences.zh: 舊曆置日餘而求朏朒之數，衰次不倫。

translations.literal: The old calendar set day remainder to seek crescent-gibbous numbers—the declining ranks were disordered.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendar derived crescent-gibbous figures from day remainders, producing disordered declining ranks.

sentences.zh: 今從其度而遲疾有漸，月之課驗，稍符天度。

translations.literal: Now following its degrees, slow-fast has gradation; the moon's examination and test slightly matches celestial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Now following its degrees with gradual slow-fast change, lunar verification aligns more closely with the heavens.

sentences.zh: 轉度母：轉法、會周附。

translations.literal: Rotation-degree mother: rotation method and conjunction cycle attached.
translations.idiomatic: Rotation-degree mother: see attached rotation method and conjunction cycle.

sentences.zh: 本以朔分並周天，是為會周。

translations.literal: Originally taking new-moon fraction joined with circuit of heaven—this is the conjunction cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the new-moon fraction was added to the circuit of heaven to form the conjunction cycle.

sentences.zh: 一朔之月常度也，名周本母。

translations.literal: One new moon's monthly mean degree—named circuit root mother.
translations.idiomatic: This is one new moon's normal monthly arc, called the circuit root mother.

sentences.zh: 去其朔差為轉終，朔差乃終外之數也。

translations.literal: Remove its new-moon difference for rotation end; the new-moon difference is the number outside the end.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the new-moon difference to obtain the rotation endpoint; the new-moon difference is the excess beyond the endpoint.

sentences.zh: 各以等數約之，即得實用之數。

translations.literal: Each by equal numbers reduce it—then obtain the practically used numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce each by common divisors to obtain the practical figures.

sentences.zh: 乃以等數約本母為轉度母，齊數也。

translations.literal: Then by equal numbers reduce the root mother to rotation-degree mother—aligned numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The root mother is then reduced by common divisors to become the rotation-degree mother—aligned figures.

sentences.zh: 又以等數約月分為轉法，亦名轉日法也。

translations.literal: Again by equal numbers reduce monthly fraction to rotation method—also named rotation day method.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly fraction is similarly reduced to form the rotation divisor, also called the rotation day divisor.

sentences.zh: 以轉法約轉終，得轉日及餘。

translations.literal: By rotation method reduce rotation end, obtaining rotation days and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the rotation endpoint by the rotation divisor yields rotation days and remainder.

sentences.zh: 本曆創立此數，皆古曆所未有。

translations.literal: This calendar originally established these numbers—all not found in ancient calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar first established these quantities, unknown in older calendars.

sentences.zh: 約得八千一百一十二萬為轉度母，二百九十八億八千二百二十四萬二千二百五十一為轉終分，三百二十億二千五百一十二萬九千二百五十一為會周，一十億八千四百四十七萬三千為轉法，二十一億四千二百八十八萬七千為朔差。

translations.literal: Reducing, we obtain 81,120,000 as rotation-degree mother, 29,882,422,251 as rotation-end fraction, 32,025,129,251 as conjunction cycle, 1,084,473,000 as rotation method, 2,142,887,000 as new-moon difference.
translations.idiomatic: The reduced values are: rotation-degree mother 81,120,000; rotation-end fraction 29,882,422,251; conjunction cycle 32,025,129,251; rotation divisor 1,084,473,000; new-moon difference 2,142,887,000.

sentences.zh: 月離遲疾定差：《皇極》有加減限、朏朒積，《麟德》曰增減率、遲疾積，《大衍》曰損益率、朏朒積，《崇天》亦曰損益率、朏朒積。

translations.literal: Lunar departure slow-fast fixed difference: the Imperial Ultimate had increase-decrease limit and crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Qilin Virtue called them increase-decrease rate and slow-fast accumulation; the Great Expansion increase-decrease rate and crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Honoring Heaven also increase-decrease rate and crescent-gibbous accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar motion slow-fast fixed difference: the Huangji used increase-decrease limit and crescent-gibbous accumulation; the Lindé used increase-decrease rate and slow-fast accumulation; the Dayan and Chongtian used increase-decrease rate and crescent-gibbous accumulation.

sentences.zh: 所謂日不及平行則損之，過平行則益之，從陽之義也；

translations.literal: What is called: when the sun does not reach mean motion then decrease it; passing mean motion then increase it—the meaning following yang;
translations.idiomatic: When the sun falls short of mean motion it is decreased; when it exceeds mean motion it is increased—following the principle of yang;

sentences.zh: 月不及平行則益之，過平行則損之，禦陰之道也。

translations.literal: when the moon does not reach mean motion then increase it; passing mean motion then decrease it—the way of governing yin.
translations.idiomatic: when the moon falls short it is increased, and when it exceeds it is decreased—the way of governing yin.

sentences.zh: 陰陽相錯而以損益、遲疾為名。

translations.literal: Yin and yang cross each other, yet naming increase-decrease and slow-fast.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang interlock, hence the names increase-decrease and slow-fast.

sentences.zh: 新曆以一萬四千八百一十九為遲疾之極，而得五度八分，其數與躔相錯，可以知合食加時之早晚也。

translations.literal: The new calendar takes 14,819 as the pole of slow-fast, obtaining 5 degrees 8 fen; its number crosses with lodge motion—one can know conjunction and eclipse addition-time early or late.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar sets 14,819 as the slow-fast maximum, yielding 5°8′; this figure interlocks with lodge motion to determine whether conjunctions and eclipses occur early or late.

sentences.zh: 進朔：進朔之法，興於《麟德》。

translations.literal: Advancing new moon: the method of advancing new moon arose in the Qilin Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing new moon: the advancing-new-moon method originated in the Lindé calendar.

sentences.zh: 自後諸曆，因而立法，互有不同。

translations.literal: Calendars thereafter each accordingly made laws—mutually having differences.
translations.idiomatic: Later calendars each legislated accordingly, with differing rules.

sentences.zh: 假令仲夏月朔月行極疾之時，合朔當於亥正，若不進朔，則晨而月見東方；

translations.literal: Suppose at midsummer month's new moon when the moon's motion is extremely fast, conjunction should fall at the hai quarter—if not advancing new moon, then at dawn the moon is seen in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose at midsummer new moon, when lunar motion is fastest, conjunction falls at the hai quarter; without advancing the new moon, the moon would be visible in the east at dawn;

sentences.zh: 若從《大衍》，當戌初進朔，則朔日之夕，月生於西方。

translations.literal: If following the Great Expansion, it should advance at xu initial—then on new-moon day's evening, the moon is born in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Dayan method, advancing at xu initial, the moon would rise in the west on new-moon evening.

sentences.zh: 新曆察朔日之餘，驗月行徐疾，變立法率，參驗加時，常視定朔小餘：秋分後四分法之三已上者，進一日；

translations.literal: The new calendar inspects the new-moon day's remainder, tests the moon's motion slow-fast, changes and establishes the legislative rate, cross-checks the addition time, always viewing the fixed new moon's small remainder: after autumn equinox, three-fourths of the quarter method and above—advance one day;
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar examines the new-moon remainder, tests lunar slow-fast motion, sets a variable rate, and checks the hour of conjunction, always judging the fixed new moon's small remainder: after the autumn equinox, if it reaches three-fourths of the quarter method or more, advance one day;

sentences.zh: 春分後定朔晨分差如春分之日者，三約之，以減四分之二；

translations.literal: after spring equinox, if the fixed new moon's dawn difference equals the spring equinox day, reduce by three-fifths, subtracting two-fourths;
translations.idiomatic: after the spring equinox, if the fixed-new-moon dawn difference equals that on the equinox day, take two-thirds of two-fourths as the threshold;

sentences.zh: 定朔小餘如此數已上者，亦進，以來日為朔。

translations.literal: if the fixed new moon's small remainder reaches such a number and above, also advance, taking the coming day as new moon.
translations.idiomatic: if the fixed new moon's small remainder meets this threshold or more, advance likewise, making the following day the new moon.

sentences.zh: 俾迴圈合度，月不見於朔晨；

translations.literal: Thus the cycle returns to combined degrees, and the moon is not seen at new-moon dawn;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the cycle aligns with combined degrees so the moon is not visible at new-moon dawn;

sentences.zh: 交會無差，明必藏於朔夕。

translations.literal: conjunction without discrepancy—the bright must be hidden at new-moon evening.
translations.idiomatic: conjunctions stay accurate, and the moon is hidden at new-moon dusk.

sentences.zh: 加時在於午中，則晦日之晨同二日之夕，皆合月見；

translations.literal: When the addition time falls at noon, then the last day's dawn and the second day's evening alike show the moon;
translations.idiomatic: When conjunction falls at noon, the moon is visible both at dawn on the last day and at dusk on the second day;

sentences.zh: 加時在於酉中，則晦日之晨尚見，二日之夕未生；

translations.literal: when the addition time falls at the you quarter, then the last day's dawn is still seen, the second day's evening not yet born;
translations.idiomatic: when it falls at the you quarter, the moon is still visible at dawn on the last day but has not yet risen at dusk on the second day;

sentences.zh: 加時在於子中，則晦日之晨不見，二日之夕以生。

translations.literal: when the addition time falls at the zi quarter, then the last day's dawn is not seen, the second day's evening is born.
translations.idiomatic: when it falls at the zi quarter, the moon is not seen at dawn on the last day but has risen by dusk on the second day.

sentences.zh: 定晦朔，乃月見之晨夕可知；

translations.literal: Fixing last day and new moon, then the moon's dawn and evening visibility can be known;
translations.idiomatic: With fixed last day and new moon, the moon's visibility at dawn and dusk can be known;

sentences.zh: 課小余，則加時之早晏無失。

translations.literal: tabulating the small remainder, then the addition time's early or late is without loss.
translations.idiomatic: and tabulating the small remainder keeps the hour of conjunction accurate.

sentences.zh: 使坦然不惑，觸類而明之。

translations.literal: Making it plainly without confusion, touching categories and making them clear.
translations.idiomatic: The method is transparent and applies consistently throughout.

sentences.zh: 消息數：因漏刻立名，義通晷景。

translations.literal: Waxing-waning numbers: taking name from clepsydra marks, meaning connecting with gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Waxing-waning numbers: named from clepsydra graduations, equivalent to gnomon shadow measurement.

sentences.zh: 《麟德》曆差曰屈伸率。

translations.literal: The Qilin Virtue calendar's difference was called bending-stretching rate.
translations.idiomatic: The Lindé calendar termed the difference the bending-stretching rate.

sentences.zh: 天晝夜者，《易》進退之象也。

translations.literal: Heaven's day and night—the Changes' advance-retreat image.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night in heaven embody the Changes' image of advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 冬至一陽爻生而晷道漸升，夜漏益減，象君子之道長，故曰息；

translations.literal: At winter solstice one yang line is born and the shadow path gradually rises, night clepsydra increasingly diminishes—image of the noble man's Way growing, hence called waxing;
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice a yang line is born, shadows gradually shorten, and night clepsydra marks decrease—emblematic of the noble Way growing, hence called waxing;

sentences.zh: 夏至一陰爻生，而晷道漸降，夜漏益增，象君子之道消，故曰消。

translations.literal: at summer solstice one yin line is born, and the shadow path gradually descends, night clepsydra increasingly increases—image of the noble man's Way waning, hence called waning.
translations.idiomatic: at the summer solstice a yin line is born, shadows lengthen, and night clepsydra marks increase—emblematic of the noble Way waning, hence called waning.

sentences.zh: 表景與陽為沖，從晦者也，故與夜漏長短。

translations.literal: The gnomon shadow opposes yang, following the obscure—hence it accords with night clepsydra long and short.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow opposes yang and follows the obscure, hence it tracks the length of night clepsydra marks.

sentences.zh: 今以屈伸象太陰之行，而刻差曰消息數。

translations.literal: Now using bending-stretching to image the Great Yin's motion, while clepsydra difference is called waxing-waning numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Now bending-stretching images lunar motion, while clepsydra differences are termed waxing-waning numbers.

sentences.zh: 黃道去極，日行有南北，故晷漏有長短。

translations.literal: The ecliptic departs from the pole; the sun's daily path has south and north—hence gnomon shadow and clepsydra have long and short.
translations.idiomatic: As the ecliptic departs from the pole, the sun's daily path shifts north and south, so gnomon shadows and clepsydra marks vary in length.

sentences.zh: 然景差徐疾不同者，句股使之然也。

translations.literal: Yet when shadow difference is slow-fast and not the same, right triangle legs make it so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet shadow differences vary in speed because right-triangle geometry governs them.

sentences.zh: 景直晷中則差遲，與句股數齊則差急，隨北極高下，所遇不同。

translations.literal: When the shadow is straight at the gnomon's center the difference is slow; when aligned with right-triangle numbers the difference is fast—following the north pole's height, what is encountered differs.
translations.idiomatic: When the shadow falls straight at the gnomon center the change is slow; when the right-triangle ratio applies it is fast—varying with the height of the north pole.

sentences.zh: 其黃道去極度數與日景、漏刻、昏晚中星反覆相求，消息用率，步日景而稽黃道，因黃道而生漏刻，而正中星，四術旋相為中，以合九服之變，約而易知，簡而易從。

translations.literal: Its ecliptic departure-from-pole degrees, with solar shadow, clepsydra marks, dusk-dawn, and culminating stars, repeatedly seek one another; waxing-waning applied rates step solar shadow to audit the ecliptic, from the ecliptic producing clepsydra marks, and centering culminating stars—four techniques revolving mutually as mean, to combine the nine domains' changes, concise and easy to know, simple and easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ecliptic polar distance, solar shadow, clepsydra marks, dusk-dawn, and culminating stars are solved iteratively; waxing-waning rates derive solar shadow to verify the ecliptic, clepsydra marks from the ecliptic, and culminating stars at center—four methods interlocking to harmonize regional variation, concise and easy to apply.

sentences.zh: 六十四卦：十二月卦出於孟氏，七十二候原于《周書》。

translations.literal: Sixty-four hexagrams: the twelve-month hexagrams come from the Meng clan; seventy-two hou originate from the Zhou Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four hexagrams: the twelve-month hexagrams derive from the Meng school; the seventy-two hou originate in the Documents of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 後宋景業因劉洪傳卦，李淳風據舊曆元圖，皆未睹陰陽之賾。

translations.literal: Later Song Jingye followed Liu Hong's transmitted hexagrams; Li Chunfeng relied on the old calendar's origin diagram—both had not seen yin-yang's hidden depths.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Song Jingye followed Liu Hong's hexagram transmission and Li Chunfeng relied on older origin diagrams—neither had grasped yin-yang's deeper pattern.

sentences.zh: 至開元中，浮屠一行考揚子雲《太玄經》，錯綜其數，索隱周公三統，糾正時訓，參其變通，著在爻象，非深達《易》象，孰能造於此乎！

translations.literal: By the Kaiyuan era, the monk Yixing examined Yang Xiong's Supreme Mystery, interweaving its numbers, seeking the hidden in the Duke of Zhou's Triple Concordance, correcting seasonal instruction, consulting its transformations, set forth in line images—without deeply penetrating the Changes' images, who could reach this!
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the monk Yixing studied Yang Xiong's Taixuan jing, interwove its numbers, recovered the Duke of Zhou's Triple Concordance, corrected seasonal doctrine, and embodied its transformations in the line images—only one deeply versed in the Changes could have achieved this.

sentences.zh: 今之所修，循一行舊義，至於周策分率，隨數遷變。

translations.literal: What is now revised follows Yixing's old meaning; as for the Zhou policy's fractional rates, they shift with the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The present revision follows Yixing's original scheme; the Zhou policy fractional rates change with the figures.

sentences.zh: 夫六十卦直常度全次之交者，諸侯卦也；

translations.literal: Of the sixty hexagrams, those straight at full degree and whole rank crossing are the feudal-lord hexagrams;
translations.idiomatic: Among the sixty hexagrams, those aligned with whole-degree crossings are the feudal-lord hexagrams;

sentences.zh: 竟六日三千四百八、十六秒而大夫受之；

translations.literal: after six days 3,408 and 86 seconds the grandee receives it;
translations.idiomatic: after six days 3,408 and 86 seconds the grandee receives it;

sentences.zh: 次九卿受之；

translations.literal: next the nine ministers receive it;
translations.idiomatic: next the nine ministers receive it;

sentences.zh: 次三公受之；

translations.literal: next the three dukes receive it;
translations.idiomatic: next the three dukes receive it;

sentences.zh: 次天子受之。

translations.literal: next the Son of Heaven receives it.
translations.idiomatic: next the Son of Heaven receives it.

sentences.zh: 五六相錯，復協常月之次。

translations.literal: Five and six cross each other, again harmonizing with the regular month's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five and six interlock, returning to the regular monthly sequence.

sentences.zh: 凡九三應上九，則天微然以靜；

translations.literal: Whenever nine-three responds to upper nine, then Heaven is faintly still;
translations.idiomatic: When nine-three corresponds to upper nine, Heaven grows faintly still;

sentences.zh: 六三應上六，則地鬱然而定。

translations.literal: six-three responds to upper six, then Earth is dense and settled.
translations.idiomatic: when six-three corresponds to upper six, Earth grows dense and settled.

sentences.zh: 九三應上六即溫，六三應上九即寒。

translations.literal: Nine-three responding to upper six means warmth; six-three responding to upper nine means cold.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-three with upper six brings warmth; six-three with upper nine brings cold.

sentences.zh: 上爻陽者風，陰者雨。

translations.literal: When the upper line is yang there is wind; when yin there is rain.
translations.idiomatic: A yang upper line brings wind; a yin upper line brings rain.

sentences.zh: 各視所直之爻，察不刊之象，而知五等與君辟之得失、過與不及焉。

translations.literal: Each views the line it governs, examines the unfailing images, and knows the five ranks' and ruler's gain and loss, excess and shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Observe the governing line and its fixed images to read the five ranks' and the ruler's gains and losses, excess and deficiency.

sentences.zh: 七十二候，李業興以來迄於《麟德》，凡七家曆，皆以雞始乳為立春初候，東風解凍為次候，其餘以次承之。

translations.literal: Seventy-two hou: from Li Yexing through the Qilin Virtue, seven calendar families in all all took hens beginning to brood as the first hou of Establishing Spring, east wind thawing ice as the second hou—the rest followed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two hou: from Li Yexing through the Lindé, seven calendar traditions all took hens beginning to brood as the first Establishing Spring hou and thawing east wind as the second—the rest followed in sequence.

sentences.zh: 與《周書》相校，二十餘日，舛訛益甚。

translations.literal: Compared with the Zhou Documents, more than twenty days—errors and mistakes ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the Documents of Zhou, they were off by more than twenty days, with ever greater errors.

sentences.zh: 而一行改從古義，今亦以《周書》為正。

translations.literal: Yet Yixing changed to follow ancient meaning; now also the Zhou Documents are taken as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing reverted to ancient usage; the present revision likewise takes the Documents of Zhou as authoritative.

sentences.zh: 嶽台日晷：岳台者，今京師嶽台坊，地曰浚儀，近古候景之所。

translations.literal: Yue Terrace solar gnomon: Yue Terrace is today's capital Yue Terrace ward, the place called Junyi—near the ancient site for observing shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Terrace gnomon: Yue Terrace is present-day Yue Terrace ward in the capital, at Junyi—the ancient shadow-observation site.

sentences.zh: 《尚書·洛誥》稱東土是也。

translations.literal: The Documents' Luo Announcement calls this the eastern land.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents' Luo Announcement identifies this as the eastern domain.

sentences.zh: 《禮》玉人職：「土圭長尺有五寸以致日。」

translations.literal: The Rites' jade-worker office: "The earth gnomon is one chi five cun long to reach the sun."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites' jade-worker statute: "The earth gnomon is one chi and five cun long to reach the sun."

sentences.zh: 此即日有常數也。

translations.literal: This is the sun's having constant numbers.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the sun has fixed measures.

sentences.zh: 司徒職以圭正日晷，「日至之景，尺有五寸，謂之地中。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works' office used the gnomon to correct the solar gnomon: "At solstice the shadow, one chi five cun, is called the earth's center."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works used the gnomon to correct the solar dial: "At solstice the shadow of one chi five cun marks the earth's center."

sentences.zh: 此即是地土中致日景與土圭等。

translations.literal: This is the earth's center reaching solar shadow equal to the earth gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: That is, at the earth's center the solar shadow equals the earth gnomon.

sentences.zh: 然表長八尺，見於《周髀》。

translations.literal: Yet an eight-chi table length appears in the Zhou Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet an eight-chi gnomon appears in the Zhou Bi.

sentences.zh: 夫天有常運，地有常中，曆有正象，表有定數。

translations.literal: Heaven has constant motion, earth has constant center, the calendar has correct images, the gnomon has fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has constant motion, earth a fixed center, the calendar correct images, and the gnomon fixed measures.

sentences.zh: 言日至者，明其日至此也。

translations.literal: Speaking of solstice day means making clear that solstice reaches here.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of solstice day is to mark where solstice occurs.

sentences.zh: 景尺有五寸與圭等者，是其景晷之真效。

translations.literal: Shadow one chi five cun equal to the gnomon means this is the shadow-gnomon's true effect.
translations.idiomatic: A shadow of one chi five cun matching the gnomon is the true gnomon-shadow effect.

sentences.zh: 然夏至之日尺有五寸之景，不因八尺之表將何以得？

translations.literal: Yet the summer solstice day's shadow of one chi five cun—without an eight-chi table, how would it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how could the summer solstice shadow of one chi five cun be obtained without an eight-chi gnomon?

sentences.zh: 故經見夏至日景者，明表有定數也。

translations.literal: Hence the classic's mention of summer solstice solar shadow makes clear the gnomon has fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the classic's mention of the summer solstice shadow shows the gnomon has a fixed measure.

sentences.zh: 新曆周歲中晷長短，皆以八尺之表測候，所得名中晷常數。

translations.literal: The new calendar's mid-year gnomon long and short all use an eight-chi table to measure and observe, obtaining what is named the mid-gnomon constant.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar's mid-year shadow lengths are all measured with an eight-chi gnomon, yielding what is called the mid-gnomon constant.

sentences.zh: 交會日月，成象於天，以辨尊卑之序。

translations.literal: Conjunction of sun and moon forms images in heaven, to distinguish the order of honor and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Solar and lunar conjunction forms heavenly images to distinguish the order of honor and rank.

sentences.zh: 日，君道也；

translations.literal: The sun is the lord's Way;
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the Way of the lord;

sentences.zh: 月，臣道也。

translations.literal: The moon is the minister's Way.
translations.idiomatic: The moon is the Way of the minister.

sentences.zh: 謫食之變，皆與人事相應。

translations.literal: The transformations of eclipse all correspond to human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse phenomena all correspond to human affairs.

sentences.zh: 若人君修德以禳之，則或當食而不食。

translations.literal: If the ruler cultivates virtue to avert them, then sometimes when there should be an eclipse there is none.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler cultivates virtue to avert them, a predicted eclipse may fail to occur.

sentences.zh: 故太陰有變行以避日，則不食；

translations.literal: Hence if the Great Yin has altered motion to avoid the sun, then no eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: Thus if the moon alters its course to avoid the sun, there is no eclipse;

sentences.zh: 五星潛在日下，為太陰禦侮而扶救，則不食；

translations.literal: If the five stars lurk beneath the sun, for the Great Yin to ward insult and lend rescue, then no eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: If the five planets hide below the sun to shield and aid the moon, there is no eclipse;

sentences.zh: 涉交數淺，或在陽曆，日光著盛，陰氣衰微，則不食；

translations.literal: If the crossing depth is shallow, or in the yang calendar when solar light flourishes and yin qi is faint, then no eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: If the crossing depth is shallow, or if it falls in the solar season when sunlight is strong and yin force is weak, there is no eclipse;

sentences.zh: 德之休明而有小眚焉，天為之隱，是以光微蔽之，雖交而不見食。

translations.literal: When virtue is splendid and bright yet there is a small blemish, Heaven hides it for this reason, and so the light faintly veils it; though crossing, no eclipse is seen.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue shines brightly with only a minor fault, Heaven conceals the sign—dimming the light so that though the bodies cross, no eclipse appears.

sentences.zh: 此四者，皆德感之所繇致也。

translations.literal: These four all are what virtue's influence brings about.
translations.idiomatic: These four cases all arise from the influence of virtue.

sentences.zh: 按《大衍曆議》：開元十二年七月戊午朔，當食。

translations.literal: According to the Dayan Calendar Discourse: in the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, seventh month, wuwu new moon, an eclipse was due.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourse on the Great Evolution Calendar records: at the wuwu new moon of the seventh month, Kaiyuan year 12, an eclipse was predicted.

sentences.zh: 時自交阯至朔方，同日度景測候之際，晶明無雲而不食。

translations.literal: At that time from Jiaozhi to Shuofang, on the same day while measuring shadows to observe, it was crystal clear without clouds yet no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Observations from Jiaozhi to Shuofang on that same day found clear skies and bright sun—no eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 以曆推之，其日入交七百八十四分，當食八分半。

translations.literal: By the calendar reckoned, that day entered crossing 784 parts; the eclipse should have been eight and a half parts.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar calculation gave an entry into crossing of 784 parts and a predicted eclipse of eight and a half tenths.

sentences.zh: 十三年，天正南至，東封禮畢，還次梁、宋，史官言：「十二月庚戌朔，當食。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when heaven's standard south reached, after the eastern Feng rites concluded, returning to halt at Liang and Song, the historiographer said: 'Twelfth month, gengxu new moon—an eclipse is due.'
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, after the winter solstice and the eastern Feng ceremony, while the emperor halted at Liang and Song, the historiographers reported: 'An eclipse is due on the gengxu new moon of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「予方修先後之職，謫見於天，是朕之不敏，無以對揚上帝之休也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I am just now cultivating the duties of predecessors; a celestial reproof appears in heaven—this is my lack of keenness, unable to respond and exalt Heaven's blessings.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'I am fulfilling the duties of my forebears, yet heaven shows a reproof—this reflects my own inadequacy, unworthy to answer and glorify Heaven's favor.'

sentences.zh: 於是徹膳素服以俟之，而卒不食。

translations.literal: Thereupon he removed delicacies and wore plain garments to await it, yet in the end no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: He then abolished rich fare and wore plain robes to await the event—but no eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 在位之臣莫不稱慶，以謂德之動天，不俟終日。

translations.literal: Courtiers in office all praised and celebrated, saying virtue moved heaven, not waiting for the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister in court rejoiced, declaring that virtue had moved heaven without waiting even a full day.

sentences.zh: 以曆推之，是月入交二度弱，當食十五分之十三，而陽光自若，無纖毫之變，雖算術乖舛，不宜若是。

translations.literal: By the calendar reckoned, that month entered crossing a little over two degrees; the eclipse should have been thirteen fifteenths, yet solar light was as before, without the slightest change—though reckoning may err, it ought not be like this.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar predicted entry into crossing of just over two degrees and an eclipse of thirteen-fifteenths, yet the sun remained unchanged—not a trace of dimming; reckoning may err, but not to this degree.

sentences.zh: 凡治曆之道，定分最微，故損益毫釐，未得其正，則上考《春秋》以來日月交食之載，必有所差。

translations.literal: In general the way of making calendars—fixing parts is most minute; hence increasing or decreasing by hair and grain, if not obtaining the correct, then checking records of sun-moon crossings and eclipses since the Spring and Autumn Annals, there must be some discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-making hinges on minute fractional constants; the slightest adjustment, if wrong, will misalign all solar and lunar eclipse records back through the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 假令治曆者因開元二食變交限以從之，則所協甚少，而差失過多。

translations.literal: Suppose calendar-makers altered crossing limits according to the two Kaiyuan eclipses—then what agrees would be very few, while errors would be too many.
translations.idiomatic: If calendar-makers adjusted crossing limits to fit those two Kaiyuan eclipses alone, few other predictions would agree and errors would multiply.

sentences.zh: 由此明之，《詩》云：「此日而微。」

translations.literal: From this it is clear: the Odes says, 'This day and faint.'
translations.idiomatic: This makes clear the Odes line: 'On this day the sun grew dim.'

sentences.zh: 乃非天之常數也。

translations.literal: Yet this is not heaven's constant number.
translations.idiomatic: That was not heaven's regular course.

sentences.zh: 舊曆直求月行入交，今則先課交初所在，然後與月行更相表裏，務通精數。

translations.literal: The old calendar directly sought the moon's motion entering crossing; now one first examines where crossing's beginning lies, then mutually outer and inner with the moon's motion, striving to penetrate fine numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendar simply computed when the moon entered crossing; the Tianli Calendar first determines the crossing's initial position, then interlocks it with lunar motion to achieve precise agreement.

sentences.zh: 四正食差：正交如累壁，漸減則有差。

translations.literal: Four cardinal eclipse differences: at true crossing like piled walls; gradually diminishing then there is difference.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse differences at the four cardinal points: at true crossing the paths align like a wall; as they diverge, discrepancies appear.

sentences.zh: 在內食分多，在外食分少；

translations.literal: Inside, eclipse fraction is greater; outside, eclipse fraction is less;
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses nearer the center show greater obscuration; those farther out show less;

sentences.zh: 交淺則間遙，交深則相薄；

translations.literal: Shallow crossing then interval distant; deep crossing then mutually press close;
translations.idiomatic: A shallow crossing widens the gap; a deep crossing brings the bodies close;

sentences.zh: 所觀之地又偏，所食之時亦別。

translations.literal: The place observed is also off-center, the time of eclipse also differs.
translations.idiomatic: The observer's location skews the view, and the hour of eclipse varies as well.

sentences.zh: 苟非地中，皆隨所在而漸異。

translations.literal: If not at earth's center, all gradually differ following where one is located.
translations.idiomatic: Except at the earth's center, results differ gradually with location.

sentences.zh: 縱交分正等同在南方，冬食則多，夏食乃少。

translations.literal: Even if crossing parts are equal and alike in the south, winter eclipses are more, summer eclipses then less.
translations.idiomatic: Even with identical crossing fractions in the south, winter eclipses are larger and summer eclipses smaller.

sentences.zh: 假均冬夏，早晚又殊，處南北則高，居東西則下。

translations.literal: Suppose winter and summer were equalized, morning and evening again differ; located north-south then high, situated east-west then low.
translations.idiomatic: Even averaging winter and summer, morning and evening differ; observers to the north or south see higher paths, those east or west lower.

sentences.zh: 視有斜正，理不可均。

translations.literal: Viewing has oblique and straight; in principle it cannot be uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Sight lines are oblique or direct—the phenomenon cannot be uniform.

sentences.zh: 月在陽曆，校驗古今交食，所虧不過其半。

translations.literal: The moon in the yang calendar, checking ancient and modern crossing-eclipses, what is eclipsed does not exceed half.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon is in the solar season, comparison of historical eclipses shows obscuration never exceeds half.

sentences.zh: 合置四正食差，則斜正於卯酉之間，損益於子午之位，務從親密，以考精微。

translations.literal: Combining and setting the four cardinal eclipse differences, then oblique-straight between mao and you, increase-decrease at zi and wu's positions, striving from closeness to examine fine subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Applying eclipse corrections at the four cardinal points—adjusting for obliquity between mao and you and for latitude at zi and wu—yields close agreement with fine observation.

sentences.zh: 五星立率：五星之行，亦因日而立率，以示尊卑之義。

translations.literal: Five stars establishing rates: the five stars' motion also follows the sun in establishing rates, to show the meaning of honor and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing planetary rates: the five planets' motions are likewise calibrated to the sun's motion to express the hierarchy of noble and base.

sentences.zh: 日週四時，無所不照，君道也；

translations.literal: The sun circuits the four seasons, nothing not illumined—lord's Way;
translations.idiomatic: The sun circles the four seasons and illuminates all—this is the Way of the lord;

sentences.zh: 星分行列宿，臣道也。

translations.literal: Stars separate and walk the lodges—minister's Way.
translations.idiomatic: The stars move separately through the lodges—this is the Way of the minister.

sentences.zh: 陰陽進退，於此取儀刑焉。

translations.literal: Yin-yang advance and retreat—from this one takes models and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang advance and retreat—their pattern is taken from this.

sentences.zh: 是以當陽而進，當陰而退，皆得其常，故加減之。

translations.literal: Hence when facing yang then advance, when facing yin then retreat—each obtains its regularity, therefore add and subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they advance in yang seasons and retreat in yin seasons, each according to rule—hence the additions and subtractions.

sentences.zh: 古之推步，悉皆順行，至秦方有金、火逆數。

translations.literal: Ancient stepwise reckoning all was direct motion; only by Qin were there metal and fire retrograde numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient astronomical calculation assumed only direct motion; retrograde tables for Venus and Mars appeared only in the Qin.

sentences.zh: 《大衍》曰：「木星之行與諸星稍異：商、周之際，率一百二十年而超一次；

translations.literal: The Dayan [Calendar] says: 'Jupiter's motion differs slightly from the other stars: at the Shang-Zhou boundary, the rate was 120 years to exceed one station;
translations.idiomatic: The Great Evolution Calendar states: 'Jupiter's motion differs slightly from the other planets: during the Shang and Zhou, it passed one lodge every 120 years;

sentences.zh: 至戰國之時，其行浸急；

translations.literal: by the Warring States era its motion gradually quickened;
translations.idiomatic: by the Warring States period its motion had gradually accelerated;

sentences.zh: 逮中平之後，八十四年而超一次，自此之後，以為常率。」

translations.literal: reaching after Zhongping, eighty-four years to exceed one station; from then on this was taken as the regular rate.'
