translations.idiomatic: after the Zhongping era it crossed one lodge every eighty-four years, and that has been the standard rate ever since.'

sentences.zh: 其行也，初與日合，一十八日行四度，乃晨見東方。

translations.literal: Its motion: at first conjoins the sun, in eighteen days travels four degrees, then appears at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Its cycle begins at solar conjunction; in eighteen days it travels four degrees and appears as the morning star in the east.

sentences.zh: 而順行一百八日，計行二十二度強，而留二十七日。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 108 days, reckoned travel 22 degrees strong, then stationary 27 days.
translations.idiomatic: It then moves direct for 108 days, covering just over 22 degrees, and stations for 27 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退行四十六日半，退行五度強，與日相望。

translations.literal: Then retrograde 46½ days, retrograde motion 5 degrees strong, opposite the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades for 46½ days through just over five degrees, reaching opposition with the sun.

sentences.zh: 旋日而退，又四十六日半，退五度強，復留二十七日。

translations.literal: Then with daily rotation retrograde, again 46½ days, retrograde five degrees strong, again stationary 27 days.
translations.idiomatic: It continues retrograde another 46½ days for just over five degrees and stations again for 27 days.

sentences.zh: 而順行一百八日，行十八度強，乃夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 108 days, travels eighteen degrees strong, then evening setting in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 108 more days through just over eighteen degrees and sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 又十八日行四度，復與日合。

translations.literal: Again eighteen days travels four degrees, again conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After eighteen more days and four degrees of travel it conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 火星之行：初與日合，七十日行五十二度，乃晨見東方。

translations.literal: Mars's motion: at first conjoins the sun, in seventy days travels fifty-two degrees, then appears at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Mars's cycle: it begins at solar conjunction; in seventy days it travels fifty-two degrees and appears as the morning star in the east.

sentences.zh: 而順行二百八十日，計行二百一十六度半弱，而留十一日。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 280 days, reckoned travel 216½ degrees weak, then stationary 11 days.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 280 days, covering just under 216½ degrees, and stations for 11 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退行二十九日，退九度，與日相望。

translations.literal: Then retrograde 29 days, retrograde nine degrees, opposite the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades for 29 days through nine degrees, reaching opposition with the sun.

sentences.zh: 旋日而退，又二十九日，退九度，復留十一日。

translations.literal: With daily rotation retrograde, again 29 days, retrograde nine degrees, again stationary 11 days.
translations.idiomatic: It continues retrograde another 29 days for nine degrees and stations again for 11 days.

sentences.zh: 而順行二百八十日，行一百六十四度半弱，而夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 280 days, travels 164½ degrees weak, then evening setting in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 280 more days through just under 164½ degrees and sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 又七十日，行五十二度，復與日合。

translations.literal: Again seventy days, travels fifty-two degrees, again conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After seventy more days and fifty-two degrees of travel it conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 土星之行：初與日合，二十一日行二度半，乃晨見東方。

translations.literal: Saturn's motion: at first conjoins the sun, in twenty-one days travels two and a half degrees, then appears at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn's cycle: it begins at solar conjunction; in twenty-one days it travels two and a half degrees and appears as the morning star in the east.

sentences.zh: 順行八十四日，計行九度半強，而留三十五日。

translations.literal: Direct motion 84 days, reckoned travel 9½ degrees strong, then stationary 35 days.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 84 days, covering just over nine and a half degrees, and stations for 35 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退行四十九日，退三度半，與日相望。

translations.literal: Then retrograde 49 days, retrograde three and a half degrees, opposite the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades for 49 days through three and a half degrees, reaching opposition with the sun.

sentences.zh: 乃旋日而退，又四十九日，退三度少，復留三十五日。

translations.literal: Then with daily rotation retrograde, again 49 days, retrograde three degrees less, again stationary 35 days.
translations.idiomatic: It continues retrograde another 49 days for just under three degrees and stations again for 35 days.

sentences.zh: 又順行八十四日，行七度強，而夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Again direct motion 84 days, travels seven degrees strong, then evening setting in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 84 more days through just over seven degrees and sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 又二十一日，行二度半，復與日合。

translations.literal: Again twenty-one days, travels two and a half degrees, again conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-one more days and two and a half degrees of travel it conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 金星之行：初與日合，五十八日半行四十九度太，而夕見西方。

translations.literal: Venus's motion: at first conjoins the sun, in fifty-eight and a half days travels forty-nine degrees excessive, then appears at evening in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Venus's cycle: it begins at solar conjunction; in fifty-eight and a half days it travels just over forty-nine degrees and appears as the evening star in the west.

sentences.zh: 乃順行二百三十一日，計行二百五十一度半，而留七日。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 231 days, reckoned travel 251½ degrees, then stationary 7 days.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 231 days, covering 251½ degrees, and stations for 7 days.

sentences.zh: 乃退行九日，退四度半，而夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Then retrograde 9 days, retrograde four and a half degrees, then evening setting in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades for 9 days through four and a half degrees and sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 又六日半，退四度太，與日再合。

translations.literal: Again six and a half days, retrograde four degrees excessive, again conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After six and a half more days it retrogrades just over four degrees and conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 又六日半，退四度太，而晨見東方。

translations.literal: Again six and a half days, retrograde four degrees excessive, then appears at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: After another six and a half days it retrogrades just over four degrees and appears as the morning star in the east.

sentences.zh: 又退九日，逆行四度半，而復留七日。

translations.literal: Again retrograde 9 days, retrograde motion four and a half degrees, then again stationary 7 days.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades again for 9 days through four and a half degrees and stations for 7 days.

sentences.zh: 而復順行二百三十一日，行二百五十一度半，乃晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Then again direct motion 231 days, travels 251½ degrees, then morning setting in the east.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 231 more days through 251½ degrees and sets in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 又三十八日半，行四十九度太，復與日會。

translations.literal: Again thirty-eight and a half days, travels forty-nine degrees excessive, again meets the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty-eight and a half more days and just over forty-nine degrees of travel it conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 水星之行：初與日合，十五日行三十三度，乃夕見西方。

translations.literal: Mercury's motion: at first conjoins the sun, in fifteen days travels thirty-three degrees, then appears at evening in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury's cycle: it begins at solar conjunction; in fifteen days it travels thirty-three degrees and appears as the evening star in the west.

sentences.zh: 而順行三十日，計行六十六度，而留二日，乃夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Then direct motion 30 days, reckoned travel 66 degrees, then stationary 2 days, then evening setting in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 30 days, covering 66 degrees, stations for 2 days, and sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 而退十日，退八度，與日再合。

translations.literal: Then retrograde 10 days, retrograde eight degrees, again conjoins the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades for 10 days through eight degrees and conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 又退十日，退八度，乃晨見東方，而復留三日。

translations.literal: Again retrograde 10 days, retrograde eight degrees, then appears at dawn in the east, then again stationary 3 days.
translations.idiomatic: It retrogrades another 10 days for eight degrees, appears as the morning star in the east, and stations for 3 days.

sentences.zh: 又順行三十三日，行三十三度，而晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Again direct motion 33 days, travels thirty-three degrees, then morning setting in the east.
translations.idiomatic: It moves direct for 33 more days through thirty-three degrees and sets in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 又十五日，行三十三度，與日復會。

translations.literal: Again fifteen days, travels thirty-three degrees, again meets the sun.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen more days and thirty-three degrees of travel it conjoins the sun again.

sentences.zh: 一行云：「五星伏、見、留、逆之效，表、裏、盈、縮之行，皆系之于時，驗之於政。

translations.literal: Yixing said: 'The effects of the five stars' setting, appearing, stationing, and retrograde motion, outer-inner and waxing-waning motion, all are tied to the seasons and verified in government.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said: 'The setting, appearing, stationing, and retrograde of the five planets, their outer and inner courses and waxing-waning motion, all depend on the seasons and are verified against government.

sentences.zh: 小失則小變，大失則大變；

translations.literal: Small fault then small change, great fault then great change;
translations.idiomatic: Small faults bring small changes; great faults bring great changes;

sentences.zh: 事微而象微，事章而象章。

translations.literal: Affairs slight then images slight, affairs manifest then images manifest.
translations.idiomatic: minor affairs yield minor signs; major affairs yield major signs.

sentences.zh: 蓋皇天降譴以警悟人主。

translations.literal: For august Heaven sends reproof to awaken the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven sends reproofs to awaken the ruler.

sentences.zh: 又或算者昧於象，占者迷於數，睹五星失行，悉謂之曆舛，以數象相參，兩喪其實。

translations.literal: Again some calculators are dim to images, diviners lost in numbers; seeing the five stars lose their motion, all call it calendar error—cross-referencing number and image, both lose the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Some calculators ignore celestial signs and some diviners lose themselves in numbers; seeing a planet out of place, they blame the calendar—yet cross-checking figures and omens, both miss the truth.

sentences.zh: 大凡校驗之道，必稽古今注記，使上下相距，反覆相求，苟獨異常，則失行可知矣。」

translations.literal: In general the way of verification must examine ancient and modern annotated records, making upper and lower mutually distant, repeatedly seeking one another; if alone abnormal, then lost motion can be known.'
translations.idiomatic: The proper method of verification is to consult records ancient and modern, compare distant eras, and seek repeatedly; only what remains uniquely anomalous can be called a true deviation from motion.'

sentences.zh: 星行盈縮：五星差行，惟火尤甚。

translations.literal: Star motion waxing-waning: the five stars' differential motion, only fire is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Planetary waxing and waning: all five planets vary in motion, but Mars most of all.

sentences.zh: 乃有南侵狼坐，北入匏瓜，變化超越，獨異于常，是以日行之分，自有盈縮。

translations.literal: Then there is invading south to Wolf Seat, entering north to Gourd, change and leap beyond, alone differing from the regular—hence the sun's daily parts naturally have waxing-waning.
translations.idiomatic: It may invade south to the Wolf asterism or enter north to the Gourd, changing and leaping beyond the norm—hence its daily motion naturally waxes and wanes.

sentences.zh: 此乃天度廣狹不等，氣序升降有差，考今升降之分，積為盈縮之數。

translations.literal: This is because celestial degrees' breadth and narrowness are not equal, qi sequence's rise and fall have difference; examining present rise-fall parts, accumulating them becomes waxing-waning numbers.
translations.idiomatic: This reflects unequal breadth of celestial degrees and varying rise and fall of seasonal qi; the present rise-and-fall fractions are accumulated into waxing-waning numbers.

sentences.zh: 凡五星入氣加減，興于張子信，以後方士各自增損，以求親密。

translations.literal: In general the five stars' entering qi additions and subtractions arose with Zhang Zixin; afterward technical masters each increased and decreased to seek closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Additions and subtractions for the five planets entering qi began with Zhang Zixin; later specialists each adjusted them to seek closer agreement.

sentences.zh: 而《開元曆》別為四象六爻，均以進退，今則別立盈縮，與舊異。

translations.literal: Yet the Kaiyuan Calendar separately made four images and six lines, all averaging advance-retreat; now separately establishing waxing-waning, differing from the old.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan Calendar used four images and six lines, averaging advance and retreat; the Tianli Calendar now establishes separate waxing-waning tables, differing from the old method.

sentences.zh: 五星見伏：五星見伏，皆以日度為規。

translations.literal: Five stars appearing and setting: the five stars' appearing and setting all take solar degree as rule.
translations.idiomatic: Planetary visibility: the appearing and setting of all five planets are governed by solar degree.

sentences.zh: 日度之運，既進退不常；

translations.literal: Solar degree's motion, since advance-retreat is not constant;
translations.idiomatic: Solar motion itself advances and retreats irregularly;

sentences.zh: 星行之差，亦隨而增損。

translations.literal: star motion's difference also follows in increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: planetary motion must be adjusted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 是以五星見伏，先考日度之行，今則審日行盈縮，究星躔進退，五星見伏，率皆密近。

translations.literal: Hence the five stars' appearing and setting first examine solar degree's motion; now carefully examining the sun's daily waxing-waning, investigating stars' stations advance-retreat, the five stars' appearing and setting mostly all closely agree.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly planetary visibility was reckoned from solar motion alone; the Tianli Calendar now examines the sun's daily waxing and waning and planetary advance and retreat together, so planetary visibility closely agrees with observation.

sentences.zh: 舊說，水星晨應見不見在雨水後、穀雨前，夕應見不見在處暑後、霜降前。

translations.literal: Old doctrine: Mercury morning should appear but does not between Rain Water and Grain Rain; evening should appear but does not between Limit of Heat and Frost Descent.
translations.idiomatic: Older doctrine held that Mercury failed to appear as the morning star between Rain Water and Grain Rain, and as the evening star between Limit of Heat and Frost Descent.

sentences.zh: 求天正冬至：置所求積年，以歲周乘之，為天正冬至氣積分；

translations.literal: To find heaven's first month winter solstice: set the sought accumulated years, multiply by the annual circuit—this is the heaven's first month winter solstice qi accumulated parts;
translations.idiomatic: To find the civil-year winter solstice: set the accumulated years sought, multiply by the annual circuit to obtain the winter-solstice qi accumulated parts;

sentences.zh: 滿元法除之為積日，不滿為小餘。

translations.literal: divide by the origin divisor when full to obtain accumulated days; what does not fill is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: divide by the origin divisor for accumulated days; the remainder is the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 日盈紀法去之，不盡，命甲子，算外，即得所求年前天正冬至日辰及餘。

translations.literal: discard cycle divisors per accumulated day; what remains, count from jiazi, outside the count—this obtains the sought year's prior heaven's first month winter solstice day, double-hour, and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Remove full cycle divisors from the day-count; count the remainder from jiazi beyond the count to obtain the winter solstice date, hour, and remainders for the year before the one sought.

sentences.zh: 求次氣：置天正冬至大、小餘，以氣策加之，即得次氣大、小餘。

translations.literal: To find the next qi: set the heaven's first month winter solstice large and small remainders, add the qi cycle—this obtains the next qi's large and small remainders.
translations.idiomatic: To find successive qi: set the civil winter solstice large and small remainders, add the qi cycle to obtain each next qi's large and small remainders.

sentences.zh: 若秒盈秒母從小余，小余滿元法從大余，大余滿紀法即去之。

translations.literal: If seconds fill the second mother, carry to the small remainder; if the small remainder fills the origin divisor, carry to the large remainder; if the large remainder fills the cycle divisor, discard it.
translations.idiomatic: When seconds fill the second denominator, carry into the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the origin divisor, carry into the large remainder; when the large remainder fills the cycle divisor, discard the excess.

sentences.zh: 命大餘甲子，算外，即次氣日辰及餘。

translations.literal: Count the large remainder from jiazi, outside the count—this is the next qi's day, double-hour, and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Count from jiazi on the large remainder, beyond the count, for each qi's date, hour, and remainder.

sentences.zh: 餘氣累而求之。

translations.literal: The remaining qi are found by successive accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Find the remaining qi by repeated addition.

sentences.zh: 求天正經朔：置天正冬至氣積分，滿朔實去之為積月，不盡為閏餘；

translations.literal: To find heaven's first month standard new moon: set the heaven's first month winter solstice qi accumulated parts; discard full new-moon true values for accumulated months; what does not fill is the intercalary remainder;
translations.idiomatic: To find the civil-year standard new moon: set the winter-solstice qi accumulated parts; remove full new-moon true values for accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalary remainder;

sentences.zh: 盈元法為日，不盈為餘；

translations.literal: what fills the origin divisor becomes days, what does not fill is remainder;
translations.idiomatic: full origin divisors convert to days; the remainder is the fractional part;

sentences.zh: 以減天正冬至大、小餘，為天正經朔大、小餘。

translations.literal: subtract these from the heaven's first month winter solstice large and small remainders to obtain the heaven's first month standard new moon large and small remainders.
translations.idiomatic: subtract from the civil winter solstice large and small remainders to obtain the standard new moon's large and small remainders.

sentences.zh: 大余不足減，加紀法；

translations.literal: If the large remainder is insufficient to subtract, add the cycle divisor;
translations.idiomatic: If the large remainder is too small, add the cycle divisor;

sentences.zh: 小餘不足減，退大餘，加元法以減之。

translations.literal: if the small remainder is insufficient, retreat one from the large remainder and add the origin divisor before subtracting.
translations.idiomatic: if the small remainder is too small, borrow one from the large remainder and add the origin divisor, then subtract.

sentences.zh: 命大餘甲子，算外，即得所求年前天正經朔日辰及餘。

translations.literal: Count the large remainder from jiazi, outside the count—this obtains the sought year's prior heaven's first month standard new moon day, double-hour, and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Count from jiazi on the large remainder, beyond the count, to obtain the standard new moon date, hour, and remainders for the year before the one sought.

sentences.zh: 求弦望及次朔經日：置天正經朔大、小餘，以弦策累加之，命如前，即得弦、望及次朔經日日辰及餘。

translations.literal: To find quarter-moon, full moon, and successive standard new-moon canonical days: set the heaven's first month standard new moon large and small remainders, add the quarter-moon cycle repeatedly, count as before—this obtains quarter-moon, full moon, and successive standard new-moon canonical days, double-hours, and remainders.
translations.idiomatic: To find first quarter, full moon, and successive standard new moons: set the civil standard new moon's large and small remainders, add the quarter-moon cycle repeatedly, and count as before to obtain each event's date, hour, and remainder.

sentences.zh: 求沒日：置有沒之氣小餘，二十四氣小餘在沒限已上者，為有沒之氣。

translations.literal: To find extinction day: set the small remainder of the qi that has extinction; among the twenty-four qi, those whose small remainder is at or above the extinction limit are qi with extinction.
translations.idiomatic: To find surplus days: set the small remainder of the qi subject to extinction; any of the twenty-four qi whose small remainder reaches the extinction limit or above is a qi with surplus.

sentences.zh: 以秒母乘之，其秒從之。

translations.literal: Multiply by the second mother, with its seconds carried along.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the second denominator, carrying the seconds.

sentences.zh: 用減七十一萬二千二百二十五，余以一萬二百二十五除之為沒日，不滿為除。

translations.literal: Subtract from seven hundred twelve thousand two hundred twenty-five; divide the remainder by ten thousand two hundred twenty-five for extinction days; what does not fill is remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from 712,225; divide the remainder by 10,125 for surplus days; the remainder is the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 以沒日加其氣大餘，命甲子，算外，即其氣沒日日辰。

translations.literal: Add the extinction days to that qi's large remainder, count from jiazi, outside the count—this is that qi's extinction day and double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Add the surplus days to that qi's large remainder, count from jiazi beyond the count, and obtain the surplus day's date and hour.

sentences.zh: 求減日：置有減經朔小餘，經朔小餘不滿朔虛分者，為有減之朔。

translations.literal: To find reduction day: set the standard new moon small remainder subject to reduction; standard new moons whose small remainder does not fill the new-moon void fraction are new moons with reduction.
translations.idiomatic: To find void days: set the standard new moon small remainder subject to reduction; any standard new moon whose small remainder falls short of the new-moon void fraction is a month with a void day.

sentences.zh: 以三十乘之，滿朔虛分為減日，不滿為餘。

translations.literal: Multiply by thirty; when full of the new-moon void fraction this yields reduction days; what does not fill is remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 30; divide by the new-moon void fraction for void days; the remainder is the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 以減日加經朔大餘，命甲子，算外，即其月減日日辰。

translations.literal: Add the reduction days to the standard new moon large remainder, count from jiazi, outside the count—this is that month's reduction day and double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Add the void days to the standard new moon's large remainder, count from jiazi beyond the count, and obtain that month's void-day date and hour.

sentences.zh: 秒母：一十八。

translations.literal: Second mother: eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Second denominator: 18.

sentences.zh: 求七十二候：各置中節大、小餘命之，為初候；

translations.literal: To find the seventy-two hou: for each, set the mid-season node's large and small remainders and count them—this is the initial hou;
translations.idiomatic: To find the seventy-two pentads: for each mid-season node, set its large and small remainders and count them as the first pentad;

sentences.zh: 以候策加之，為次候；

translations.literal: add the hou cycle to obtain the next hou;
translations.idiomatic: add the pentad cycle for the second pentad;

sentences.zh: 又加之，為末候。

translations.literal: add again for the final hou.
translations.idiomatic: add again for the third pentad.

sentences.zh: 各命甲子，算外，即得其候日辰。

translations.literal: For each, count from jiazi, outside the count—this obtains its hou day and double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: For each, count from jiazi beyond the count to obtain the pentad's date and hour.

sentences.zh: 求六十四卦：各因中氣大、小餘命之，為公卦用事日；

translations.literal: To find the sixty-four hexagrams: for each, take the mid-qi large and small remainders and count them—this is the duke hexagram's dominion day;
translations.idiomatic: To find the sixty-four hexagrams: for each mid-qi, set its large and small remainders and count them as the duke hexagram's dominion day;

sentences.zh: 以卦策加之，即次卦用事日；

translations.literal: add the hexagram cycle to obtain the next hexagram's dominion day;
translations.idiomatic: add the hexagram cycle to obtain the next hexagram's dominion day;

sentences.zh: 以土王策加諸侯之卦，得十有二節之初外卦用事日。

translations.literal: add the earth-king cycle to the feudal lords' hexagram to obtain the outer hexagram's dominion day at the start of each of the twelve nodes.
translations.idiomatic: add the earth-king cycle to the feudal-lord hexagram to obtain the outer hexagram's dominion day at the opening of each of the twelve seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 求五行用事日：各因四立之節大、小餘命之，即春木、夏火、秋金、冬水首用事日；

translations.literal: To find the five phases' dominion days: for each, take the four establishment nodes' large and small remainders and count them—these are spring Wood, summer Fire, autumn Metal, and winter Water first dominion days;
translations.idiomatic: To find the five phases' dominion days: for each of the four establishment nodes, set its large and small remainders and count them—the opening dominion days of spring Wood, summer Fire, autumn Metal, and winter Water;

sentences.zh: 以土王策減四季中氣大、小餘，命甲子，算外，即其月土始用事日也。

translations.literal: subtract the earth-king cycle from each season's mid-qi large and small remainders, count from jiazi, outside the count—this is that month's day when Earth first takes dominion.
translations.idiomatic: subtract the earth-king cycle from each seasonal mid-qi's large and small remainders, count from jiazi beyond the count, and obtain the day when Earth begins its dominion that month.

sentences.zh: 求發斂加時：各置小余，滿辰法除之為辰數，不滿者，刻法而一為刻，又不滿為分。

translations.literal: To find emission-contraction added time: for each, set the small remainder; divide by the double-hour divisor when full for double-hour count; what does not fill, divide by the clepsydra-mark divisor for one mark; what still does not fill is fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find emission-contraction time-of-day: set the small remainder; divide by the double-hour divisor for the double-hour count; the remainder divided by the clepsydra-mark divisor gives marks; any remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命辰數從子正，算外，即得所求加時辰時。

translations.literal: Count the double-hour number from midnight zi, outside the count—this obtains the sought added-time double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Count from midnight zi on the double-hour number, beyond the count, to obtain the true hour sought.

sentences.zh: 若以半辰之數加而命之，即得辰初後所入刻數。

translations.literal: If one adds the half double-hour number and counts, one obtains the clepsydra marks entered after the double-hour's opening.
translations.idiomatic: If one adds the half double-hour value before counting, one obtains the clepsydra marks elapsed after the hour's opening.

sentences.zh: 求發斂去經朔：置天正經朔閏餘，以月閏累加之，即每月閏餘；

translations.literal: To find emission-contraction offset from standard new moon: set the heaven's first month standard new moon intercalary remainder, add the monthly intercalation repeatedly—this is each month's intercalary remainder;
translations.idiomatic: To find emission-contraction offset from the standard new moon: set the civil standard new moon's intercalary remainder and add the monthly intercalation repeatedly to obtain each month's intercalary remainder;

sentences.zh: 滿元法除之為閏日，不盡為小餘，即得其月中氣去經朔日及餘秒。

translations.literal: divide by the origin divisor when full for intercalary days; what does not fill is the small remainder—this obtains that month's mid-qi offset from the standard new moon in days, remainder, and seconds.
translations.idiomatic: divide by the origin divisor for intercalary days; the remainder is the small remainder—thus obtaining each month's mid-qi offset from the standard new moon in days, parts, and seconds.

sentences.zh: 其閏余滿閏限，即為置閏，以月內無中氣為定。

translations.literal: When its intercalary remainder fills the intercalation limit, intercalation is inserted, determined by a month lacking mid-qi within it.
translations.idiomatic: When the intercalary remainder reaches the intercalation limit, insert an intercalary month, confirmed by a month that contains no mid-qi.

sentences.zh: 求卦候去經朔：各以卦、候策及餘秒累加減之，中氣前，減；

translations.literal: To find hexagram and hou offset from standard new moon: for each, add or subtract the hexagram and hou cycles with remainder and seconds cumulatively; before mid-qi, subtract;
translations.idiomatic: To find hexagram and pentad offset from the standard new moon: for each, cumulatively add or subtract the hexagram and pentad cycles with remainders and seconds; before mid-qi, subtract;

sentences.zh: 中氣後，加。

translations.literal: after mid-qi, add.
translations.idiomatic: after mid-qi, add.

sentences.zh: 即各得卦、候去經朔日及餘秒。

translations.literal: Thus for each one obtains the hexagram and hou offset from the standard new moon in days, remainder, and seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Thus obtain each hexagram and pentad's offset from the standard new moon in days, parts, and seconds.

sentences.zh: 求朔弦望入盈縮度：置二至限度及餘，以天正閏日及餘減之，余為天正經朔入縮度及餘；

translations.literal: To find new moon, quarter-moon, and full moon entry into expansion-contraction degrees: set the solstitial limit and remainder, subtract the heaven's first month intercalary day and remainder—the remainder is the heaven's first month standard new moon entry into contraction degrees and remainder;
translations.idiomatic: To find entry into expansion-contraction for new moon, quarters, and full moon: set the solstitial limit and remainder, subtract the civil intercalary day and remainder—the remainder is the standard new moon's entry into contraction degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 以弦策累加之，滿二至限度及餘去之，則盈入縮，縮入盈而互得之。

translations.literal: add the quarter-moon cycle repeatedly; discard the solstitial limit and remainder when full—then expansion enters contraction and contraction enters expansion, obtained alternately.
translations.idiomatic: add the quarter-moon cycle repeatedly; remove the solstitial limit when full—expansion then yields to contraction and contraction to expansion in alternation.

sentences.zh: 即得弦、望及次經朔日所入盈縮度及餘。

translations.literal: Thus one obtains the expansion-contraction degrees and remainder entered on quarter-moon, full moon, and successive standard new-moon days.
translations.idiomatic: Thus obtain the expansion-contraction degrees and parts for each quarter, full moon, and successive standard new moon.

sentences.zh: 其餘以一萬乘之，元法除之，即得約分。

translations.literal: Multiply its remainder by ten thousand and divide by the origin divisor—this yields the reduced fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the remainder by 10,000 and divide by the origin divisor to obtain the reduced fraction.

sentences.zh: 求朔弦望盈縮差及定差：各置朔、弦、望所入盈縮度及約分，如在象度分以下者為在初；

translations.literal: To find new moon, quarter-moon, and full moon expansion-contraction difference and fixed difference: for each, set the expansion-contraction degrees and reduced fraction entered at new moon, quarter-moon, or full moon; if below the quadrant-degree fraction, it is in the initial portion;
translations.idiomatic: To find expansion-contraction difference and true correction for new moon, quarters, and full moon: set the entered expansion-contraction degrees and reduced fraction; if below the quadrant-degree fraction, the position is in the initial portion;

sentences.zh: 已上者，覆減二至限，餘為在末。

translations.literal: if at or above, reverse-subtract the solstitial limit; the remainder is in the final portion.
translations.idiomatic: if at or above, subtract from the solstitial limit in reverse; the remainder places it in the final portion.

sentences.zh: 置初、末度分於上，列二至於下，以上減下，餘以下乘上，為積數；

translations.literal: Place the initial or final degree-fraction above and list the solstice below; subtract the lower from the upper; multiply the remainder by the upper—this is the accumulated number;
translations.idiomatic: Place the initial or final degree-fraction above and the solstitial value below; subtract the lower from the upper; multiply the remainder by the upper to obtain the accumulated product;

sentences.zh: 滿四千一百三十五除之為度，不滿，退除為分，命曰盈縮差度及分。

translations.literal: divide by four thousand one hundred thirty-five when full for degrees; what does not fill, retreat one step and divide for fractional parts—named the expansion-contraction difference in degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: divide by 4,135 for degrees; the remainder, reduced one place, gives fractional parts—the expansion-contraction difference in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 若以四百乘積數，滿五百六十七除之，為盈縮定差。

translations.literal: If one multiplies the accumulated number by four hundred and divides by five hundred sixty-seven when full, this is the expansion-contraction fixed difference.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying the accumulated product by 400 and dividing by 567 yields the true expansion-contraction correction.

sentences.zh: 若用立成者，以其度損益率乘度除，滿元法而一，所得，以損益其度下盈縮積，為定差度；

translations.literal: If using ready reckoning, multiply the degree's increase-decrease rate by the degree divisor, divide by the origin divisor and take one—what is obtained is used to increase or decrease the expansion-contraction accumulation below that degree, yielding the fixed-difference degree;
translations.idiomatic: With precomputed tables, multiply the degree's increase-decrease rate by the degree divisor, divide by the origin divisor, and apply the result to adjust the expansion-contraction accumulation below that degree for the true correction;

sentences.zh: 其損益初、末分為二日者，各隨其初、末以乘除。

translations.literal: Where the increase-decrease initial and final fractions span two days, multiply and divide according to each initial and final portion.
translations.idiomatic: Where initial and final correction fractions span two days, apply multiplication and division according to each portion.

sentences.zh: 其後皆如此例。

translations.literal: Thereafter all follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: All subsequent cases follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 求定氣日：冬、夏二至，盈縮之端，以常為定。

translations.literal: To find fixed qi days: winter and summer solstices are the endpoints of expansion-contraction; the mean value is taken as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: To find true qi dates: winter and summer solstices mark the endpoints of solar anomaly; the mean date stands as the true date.

sentences.zh: 餘者以其氣所得盈縮差度及分盈減縮加常氣日及約分，即為其氣定日及分。

translations.literal: For the rest, take that qi's obtained expansion-contraction difference in degrees and parts—subtract in expansion, add in contraction—from the mean qi day and reduced fraction; this is that qi's fixed day and fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For the remaining qi, subtract the expansion-contraction difference in expansion and add it in contraction from the mean qi date and reduced fraction to obtain each qi's true date and parts.

sentences.zh: 前皆赤道度，自《大衍》以下，以儀測定，用為常數。

translations.literal: All the foregoing are equatorial degrees; from the Dayan calendar onward they were fixed by armillary measurement and adopted as standard constants.
translations.idiomatic: The figures above are all equatorial arc-degrees; from the Dayan calendar on, they were determined by instrument observation and taken as fixed constants.

sentences.zh: 赤道者，常道也，紘於天半，以格黃道。

translations.literal: The equator is the constant path; it girdles heaven's half to frame the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The equator is the unchanging track, running round the celestial middle to bracket the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 求天正冬至赤道日度：以歲差乘所求積年，滿周天分去之，不盡，用減周天分，餘以度母除之，一度為度，不滿為餘。

translations.literal: To find the civil new-year winter solstice equatorial solar degree: multiply precession by the accumulated years sought; discard full circuits of the universal divisor; what remains, subtract from the universal divisor; divide the remainder by the degree mother — each full unit is one degree, what does not fill is the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun's equatorial longitude at winter solstice of civil new year: multiply the precession constant by the years sought, remove whole circuits of the universal divisor, subtract the remainder from the universal divisor, then divide by the degree mother — the quotient is degrees and the remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 余以一萬乘之，度母退除為約分。

translations.literal: Multiply the remainder by ten thousand; withdraw the degree mother by division to obtain reduced parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fractional remainder by ten thousand and divide back through the degree mother to obtain reduced fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命起赤道虛宿六度去之，至不滿宿，即所求年天正冬至加時赤道日躔所在宿度及分。

translations.literal: Assign from Emptiness lodge 6° on the equator and subtract repeatedly until less than one lodge — that is the lodge degree and parts where the sun's equatorial station at hour-added civil new-year winter solstice falls in the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Count from Void lodge at 6° on the equator and subtract lodge widths until less than one lodge remains — the result is the equatorial lodge, degrees, and parts of the sun's position at hour-added winter solstice for the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求夏至赤道加時日度：置天正冬至加時赤道日度，以二至限度及分加之，滿赤道宿度去之，即得夏至加時赤道日度。

translations.literal: To find summer solstice equatorial solar degree at hour-added time: set the civil new-year winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree, add the solstice limit in degrees and parts, discard full equatorial lodge degrees — that yields summer solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: For the summer solstice equatorial longitude at hour-added time: take the winter solstice hour-added equatorial degree, add the solstice-interval limit in degrees and parts, and discard whole equatorial lodge circuits to obtain the summer solstice hour-added equatorial degree.

sentences.zh: 若求二至昏後夜半赤道日度者，各以二至之日約餘減一萬分，餘以加二至加時赤道日度，即為二至初日昏後夜半赤道日度，每日加一度，滿赤道宿度去之，即得每日昏後夜半赤道日度。

translations.literal: If one seeks equatorial solar degrees for after dusk and midnight at the two solstices: for each, subtract the reduced remainder of that solstice day from ten thousand parts, add the remainder to the solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — that is the after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar degree on the solstice's first day; add one degree daily, discarding full equatorial lodge degrees, to obtain after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar degrees for each day.
translations.idiomatic: To derive after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar longitudes at the solstices: subtract each solstice day's reduced remainder from ten thousand parts and add what remains to the solstice hour-added equatorial degree — this gives the first solstice day's after-dusk and midnight equatorial longitude; then add one degree per day, discarding full lodge circuits, for each subsequent day.

sentences.zh: 求赤道宿積度：置冬至加時赤道宿全度，以冬至赤道加時日度減之，餘為距後度及分；

translations.literal: To find equatorial lodge accumulated degrees: set the full degree of the winter solstice hour-added equatorial lodge, subtract the winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — the remainder is the post-distance in degrees and parts;
translations.idiomatic: To find accumulated equatorial longitude by lodge: set the full width of the winter solstice hour-added equatorial lodge, subtract the winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — the remainder is the post-distance in degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 以赤道宿度累加之，即各得赤道其宿積度及分。

translations.literal: Add equatorial lodge degrees cumulatively — thus obtain each lodge's accumulated equatorial degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Add equatorial lodge widths cumulatively to obtain each lodge's accumulated equatorial degree and parts.

sentences.zh: 求赤道宿積度入初末限，各置赤道宿積度及分，滿九十一度三十一分去之，餘在四十五度六十五分半以下分以日為母。

translations.literal: To find whether equatorial accumulated lodge degrees fall in the initial or terminal limit: for each, set accumulated equatorial degrees and parts; discard multiples of 91° 31′; if the remainder is 45° 65½′ or below, parts take the day as denominator.
translations.idiomatic: To determine whether an accumulated equatorial longitude falls in the first or last limit band: set the accumulated degree and parts, remove multiples of 91° 31′; if the remainder is 45° 65½′ or less, use the day-count as denominator for the fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 為在初限；

translations.literal: then it is in the initial limit;
translations.idiomatic: It lies in the initial limit;

sentences.zh: 以上者，用減九十一度三十一分，餘為入末限度及分。

translations.literal: if above that, subtract from 91° 31′ — the remainder is entry into the terminal limit in degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: if above that threshold, subtract from 91° 31′; the remainder is the entry into the terminal limit in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 求二十八宿黃道度：各置赤道宿入初、末限度及分，用減一百一十一度三十七分，余以乘初、末限度及分，進一位，以一萬約之，所得，命曰黃赤道差度及分；

translations.literal: To find the twenty-eight lodges' ecliptic degrees: for each set the equatorial lodge's initial or terminal limit-entry in degrees and parts, subtract from 111° 37′, multiply the remainder by the initial or terminal limit-entry in degrees and parts, advance one place, reduce by ten thousand — name the result ecliptic–equator difference in degrees and parts;
translations.idiomatic: To find ecliptic arc-degrees for the twenty-eight lodges: set each lodge's initial- or terminal-limit entry, subtract from 111° 37′, multiply the remainder by that limit entry, shift one decimal place, and reduce by ten thousand — the result is the ecliptic–equator difference in degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 在至後、分前減，在分後、至前加，皆加減赤道宿積度及分，為其宿黃道積度及分；

translations.literal: after a solstice and before the equinox node, subtract; after the node and before the solstice, add — in all cases add or subtract from the equatorial accumulated lodge degree and parts to obtain that lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree and parts;
translations.idiomatic: after a solstice and before the equinox fraction, subtract; after the equinox fraction and before the solstice, add — apply this to the equatorial accumulated longitude to obtain each lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree and parts;

sentences.zh: 以前宿黃道積度減其宿黃道積度，為其宿黃道度及分。

translations.literal: Subtract the prior lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree from this lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree — that is this lodge's ecliptic degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the preceding lodge's ecliptic accumulated longitude from this lodge's to obtain that lodge's ecliptic width in degrees and parts.

translations.literal: The fractional parts are rounded nearest to greater, half, or lesser.
translations.idiomatic: Fractional parts are rounded to the nearest greater, half, or lesser step.

translations.idiomatic: If above that, subtract from the solstice-interval limit in reverse — the remainder lies in the terminal band.

sentences.zh: 置初、末度分於上，列二至於下，以上減下，餘以下乘上，為積數；

sentences.zh: 滿四千一百三十五除之為度，不滿，退除為分，命曰盈縮差度及分。

translations.literal: Divide by 4135 for degrees; what does not fill, withdraw-divide for parts — name it surplus–deficit difference in degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 4135 to obtain degrees; treat the remainder as fractional parts — this is the surplus–deficit difference in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 若以四百乘積數，滿五百六十七除之，為盈縮定差。

sentences.zh: 若用立成者，以其度損益率乘度除，滿元法而一，所得，以損益其度下盈縮積，為定差度；

translations.literal: If using the ready-made table: multiply by that degree's increase–decrease rate and divide by the degree; when it fills the origin divisor take one; add or subtract from the surplus–deficit accumulation below that degree to obtain the fixed-difference degree;
translations.idiomatic: If using the ready-made table: multiply by the increase–decrease rate for that degree, divide by the degree and by the origin divisor; apply the result to adjust the surplus–deficit accumulation under that degree to obtain the fixed correction in degrees;

sentences.zh: 其損益初、末分為二日者，各隨其初、末以乘除。

translations.literal: Where increase–decrease at initial or terminal fractions is split over two days, multiply or divide according to each initial or terminal portion.
translations.idiomatic: When the increase–decrease at an initial or terminal fraction spans two days, apply multiplication or division according to each day's initial or terminal share.

sentences.zh: 其後皆如此例。

translations.literal: Thereafter all follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent cases follow the same rule.

translations.idiomatic: To find the fixed qi day: winter and summer solstices are the endpoints of surplus–deficit variation — the mean day is taken as fixed.

sentences.zh: 前皆赤道度，自《大衍》以下，以儀測定，用為常數。

translations.literal: All the foregoing are equatorial degrees; from the Dayan calendar onward they were fixed by armillary measurement and adopted as standard constants.
translations.idiomatic: The figures above are all equatorial arc-degrees; from the Dayan calendar on, they were determined by instrument observation and taken as fixed constants.

sentences.zh: 赤道者，常道也，紘於天半，以格黃道。

translations.literal: The equator is the constant path; it girdles heaven's half to frame the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The equator is the unchanging track, running round the celestial middle to bracket the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 求天正冬至赤道日度：以歲差乘所求積年，滿周天分去之，不盡，用減周天分，餘以度母除之，一度為度，不滿為餘。

translations.literal: To find the civil new-year winter solstice equatorial solar degree: multiply precession by the accumulated years sought; discard full circuits of the universal divisor; what remains, subtract from the universal divisor; divide the remainder by the degree mother — each full unit is one degree, what does not fill is the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun's equatorial longitude at winter solstice of civil new year: multiply the precession constant by the years sought, remove whole circuits of the universal divisor, subtract the remainder from the universal divisor, then divide by the degree mother — the quotient is degrees and the remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 余以一萬乘之，度母退除為約分。

translations.literal: Multiply the remainder by ten thousand; withdraw the degree mother by division to obtain reduced parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fractional remainder by ten thousand and divide back through the degree mother to obtain reduced fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命起赤道虛宿六度去之，至不滿宿，即所求年天正冬至加時赤道日躔所在宿度及分。

translations.literal: Assign from Emptiness lodge 6° on the equator and subtract repeatedly until less than one lodge — that is the lodge degree and parts where the sun's equatorial station at hour-added civil new-year winter solstice falls in the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Count from Void lodge at 6° on the equator and subtract lodge widths until less than one lodge remains — the result is the equatorial lodge, degrees, and parts of the sun's position at hour-added winter solstice for the year sought.

sentences.zh: 求夏至赤道加時日度：置天正冬至加時赤道日度，以二至限度及分加之，滿赤道宿度去之，即得夏至加時赤道日度。

translations.literal: To find summer solstice equatorial solar degree at hour-added time: set the civil new-year winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree, add the solstice limit in degrees and parts, discard full equatorial lodge degrees — that yields summer solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: For the summer solstice equatorial longitude at hour-added time: take the winter solstice hour-added equatorial degree, add the solstice-interval limit in degrees and parts, and discard whole equatorial lodge circuits to obtain the summer solstice hour-added equatorial degree.

sentences.zh: 若求二至昏後夜半赤道日度者，各以二至之日約餘減一萬分，餘以加二至加時赤道日度，即為二至初日昏後夜半赤道日度，每日加一度，滿赤道宿度去之，即得每日昏後夜半赤道日度。

translations.literal: If one seeks equatorial solar degrees for after dusk and midnight at the two solstices: for each, subtract the reduced remainder of that solstice day from ten thousand parts, add the remainder to the solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — that is the after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar degree on the solstice's first day; add one degree daily, discarding full equatorial lodge degrees, to obtain after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar degrees for each day.
translations.idiomatic: To derive after-dusk and midnight equatorial solar longitudes at the solstices: subtract each solstice day's reduced remainder from ten thousand parts and add what remains to the solstice hour-added equatorial degree — this gives the first solstice day's after-dusk and midnight equatorial longitude; then add one degree per day, discarding full lodge circuits, for each subsequent day.

sentences.zh: 求赤道宿積度：置冬至加時赤道宿全度，以冬至赤道加時日度減之，餘為距後度及分；

translations.literal: To find equatorial lodge accumulated degrees: set the full degree of the winter solstice hour-added equatorial lodge, subtract the winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — the remainder is the post-distance in degrees and parts;
translations.idiomatic: To find accumulated equatorial longitude by lodge: set the full width of the winter solstice hour-added equatorial lodge, subtract the winter solstice hour-added equatorial solar degree — the remainder is the post-distance in degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 以赤道宿度累加之，即各得赤道其宿積度及分。

translations.literal: Add equatorial lodge degrees cumulatively — thus obtain each lodge's accumulated equatorial degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Add equatorial lodge widths cumulatively to obtain each lodge's accumulated equatorial degree and parts.

sentences.zh: 求赤道宿積度入初末限，各置赤道宿積度及分，滿九十一度三十一分去之，餘在四十五度六十五分半以下分以日為母。

translations.literal: To find whether equatorial accumulated lodge degrees fall in the initial or terminal limit: for each, set accumulated equatorial degrees and parts; discard multiples of 91° 31′; if the remainder is 45° 65½′ or below, parts take the day as denominator.
translations.idiomatic: To determine whether an accumulated equatorial longitude falls in the first or last limit band: set the accumulated degree and parts, remove multiples of 91° 31′; if the remainder is 45° 65½′ or less, use the day-count as denominator for the fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 為在初限；

translations.literal: then it is in the initial limit;
translations.idiomatic: It lies in the initial limit;

translations.literal: if above that, subtract from 91° 31′ — the remainder is entry into the terminal limit in degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: if above that threshold, subtract from 91° 31′; the remainder is the entry into the terminal limit in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 求二十八宿黃道度：各置赤道宿入初、末限度及分，用減一百一十一度三十七分，余以乘初、末限度及分，進一位，以一萬約之，所得，命曰黃赤道差度及分；

translations.literal: To find the twenty-eight lodges' ecliptic degrees: for each set the equatorial lodge's initial or terminal limit-entry in degrees and parts, subtract from 111° 37′, multiply the remainder by the initial or terminal limit-entry in degrees and parts, advance one place, reduce by ten thousand — name the result ecliptic–equator difference in degrees and parts;
translations.idiomatic: To find ecliptic arc-degrees for the twenty-eight lodges: set each lodge's initial- or terminal-limit entry, subtract from 111° 37′, multiply the remainder by that limit entry, shift one decimal place, and reduce by ten thousand — the result is the ecliptic–equator difference in degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 在至後、分前減，在分後、至前加，皆加減赤道宿積度及分，為其宿黃道積度及分；

translations.literal: after a solstice and before the equinox node, subtract; after the node and before the solstice, add — in all cases add or subtract from the equatorial accumulated lodge degree and parts to obtain that lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree and parts;
translations.idiomatic: after a solstice and before the equinox fraction, subtract; after the equinox fraction and before the solstice, add — apply this to the equatorial accumulated longitude to obtain each lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree and parts;

sentences.zh: 以前宿黃道積度減其宿黃道積度，為其宿黃道度及分。

translations.literal: Subtract the prior lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree from this lodge's ecliptic accumulated degree — that is this lodge's ecliptic degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the preceding lodge's ecliptic accumulated longitude from this lodge's to obtain that lodge's ecliptic width in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 求逐月定朔之日晨前夜半黃道日度：置其朔距冬至日數，以其度下盈縮積度盈加縮減之，餘以加天正冬至晨前夜半日度，命之，即其月定朔之日晨前夜半日躔所在宿次。

translations.literal: To find the ecliptic solar degree before dawn and at midnight on each month's fixed new-moon day: set the number of days from that new moon to winter solstice; by the surplus–deficit accumulated degree below that degree, add when in surplus and subtract when in deficit; add the remainder to the civil new-year winter solstice before-dawn and midnight solar degree, assign it — that is the lodge where the sun's station falls before dawn and at midnight on that month's fixed new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: For the ecliptic solar longitude before dawn and at midnight on each month's fixed new moon: set the days from new moon to winter solstice, apply the surplus–deficit accumulation under that degree (add in surplus, subtract in deficit), add the remainder to the civil new-year winter solstice before-dawn and midnight longitude, and assign lodges — this gives the lodge of the sun's station at that fixed new moon.

sentences.zh: 求每日晨前夜半黃道日度：各置其定朔之日晨前夜半黃道日度，每日加一度，以其日升降分升加降減之，滿黃道宿度去之，即各得每日晨前夜半黃道日躔所在宿度及分。

translations.idiomatic: For daily ecliptic longitudes before dawn and at midnight: set each fixed new moon's before-dawn and midnight ecliptic degree, add one degree per day with that day's ascending or descending parts, discard whole ecliptic lodge circuits, and obtain each day's lodge, degrees, and parts for the sun's station before dawn and at midnight.

translations.idiomatic: For the solar longitude before dawn and at midnight on the winter solstice day: set 10,000 parts, add that day's ascending parts, multiply by the winter solstice reduced remainder, and reduce by 10,000; subtract the result from the winter solstice hour-added ecliptic degree to obtain the ecliptic longitude before dawn and at midnight on that day.

sentences.zh: 求逐月定朔之日晨前夜半黃道日度：置其朔距冬至日數，以其度下盈縮積度盈加縮減之，餘以加天正冬至晨前夜半日度，命之，即其月定朔之日晨前夜半日躔所在宿次。

translations.literal: To find the ecliptic solar degree before dawn and at midnight on each month's fixed new-moon day: set the number of days from that new moon to winter solstice; by the surplus–deficit accumulated degree below that degree, add when in surplus and subtract when in deficit; add the remainder to the civil new-year winter solstice before-dawn and midnight solar degree, assign it — that is the lodge where the sun's station falls before dawn and at midnight on that month's fixed new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: For the ecliptic solar longitude before dawn and at midnight on each month's fixed new moon: set the days from new moon to winter solstice, apply the surplus–deficit accumulation under that degree (add in surplus, subtract in deficit), add the remainder to the civil new-year winter solstice before-dawn and midnight longitude, and assign lodges — this gives the lodge of the sun's station at that fixed new moon.

sentences.zh: 求每日晨前夜半黃道日度：各置其定朔之日晨前夜半黃道日度，每日加一度，以其日升降分升加降減之，滿黃道宿度去之，即各得每日晨前夜半黃道日躔所在宿度及分。

translations.literal: To find the ecliptic solar degree before dawn and at midnight for each day: for each set that month's fixed-new-moon-day before-dawn and midnight ecliptic solar degree; add one degree daily, add ascending parts or subtract descending parts for that day, discard full ecliptic lodge degrees — thus obtain for each day the lodge degree and parts where the sun's ecliptic station falls before dawn and at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: For daily ecliptic longitudes before dawn and at midnight: set each fixed new moon's before-dawn and midnight ecliptic degree, add one degree per day with that day's ascending or descending parts, discard whole ecliptic lodge circuits, and obtain each day's lodge, degrees, and parts for the sun's station before dawn and at midnight.

sentences.zh: 若次年冬至小余滿法者，以升分極數加之。

translations.literal: If the next year's winter solstice small remainder fills the divisor, add the extreme number of ascending parts.
translations.idiomatic: If the following year's winter solstice fractional remainder fills the divisor, add the maximum ascending-parts correction.
